1. OA round  [ 92 appeared ]

Platform : HackerEarth
Eligibility: CE and CSE, 7.5 CGPA cutoff
.
21 MCQ questions were asked in 50 min, primary HTML CSS JS SQL CCN questions were asked. The test was proctored and offline. The questions were easy to medium level. If you have built projects using JS it would be a piece of cake and the entire test could be completed in 30 mins max. Accuracy matters over here for clearing the cutoff.

2. Machine Coding Round [ 11 shortlisted 7 appeared ]

It was conducted in Batches offline in the BrowserStack office in Oberoi Commerz 2. Due to the limited number of students they had confined a single batch for SPIT. The PS for the machine coding round is shared below:

This problem requires you to implement a log-watching solution (similar to the tail -f command in
UNIX). However, the log file is hosted on a remote machine (same machine as your server code). The
log file is in append-only mode.
You need to implement the following:

● A server-side program to monitor the given log file and stream updates as they happen using

Socket. IO for real-time communication. This will run on the same machine as the log file. You
can use any programming language for the server.

● A web-based client (accessible via a URL like http://localhost/log) that displays updates in the

file in real-time, without requiring a page refresh. The page should load once and keep
updating. On initial load, the user should see the last 10 lines of the file.
Problem Constraints:

● The server must push updates to clients in real-time using Socket. IO.

● The log file could be several GBs. How do you optimize retrieving the last 10 lines?

● The server should not retransmit the entire file every time; it should only send updates.

● The server must handle multiple clients simultaneously.

● The web page should not stay in a loading state after the first load and should not reload

thereafter.

● You may not use off-the-shelf external libraries or tools to read the file or provide tail-like

functionalities (except Socket. IO for real-time updates).
You'll be evaluated on code quality, testability, modularity, and handling of corner cases.

The Machine coding round began at 10:30 AM and we were given roughly 2 hrs to build the backend server. You may find the solutions online, but an optimal solution that caters to the edge cases of the invigilator is preferred. You are not allowed to use any AI agents or LLMs or  medium articles during this round, our invigilator was right beside us. You may refer to the documentation for development. You can interact with the invigilator during the round. Primary goal is to develop the solution using Socket. IO , I preferred NODE for the backend and socket implementation to display logs realtime with a confined Buffer to prevent parsing the logs.
The invigilator would test it on multiple edge cases, like real time parsing, multiple browser compatibility with realtime logs and order in which they appear or cases where '\n' appears while parsing logs. If it passes all the cases and you are able to explain your code really well then you would be moved forward to the next round.

3. Director Of Engineering Round [ 3 shortlisted ]

For preparation you may go through medium or GFG articles.
Mine was an interesting one, I was the only one who had an online interview with the Senior Director in the office for 30 mins. He read my resume and given that I had worked with a corporation with exposure to multiple hacks and techstacks, was exempted from basic questions. I was asked about one of my favourite projects and what role did I play in that project. Then moved on to internship experiences, what tasks did I perform in Russell Investments as Summer Intern, what project did I work on. He asked if I had exposure to Prod and deployment which I explained pretty well. I was quickly moved to behavioral questions like how will I tackle Deadlines, How will I deal with my teammate who differs in an opinion. It was the most fun director round.

All the 3 received the offer.

Sakshi Khanna
TE ETRX
KPMG

Round 1: Aptitude Test.

This test contained 45 questions to be solved in 55 minutes. The questions were
based on Logical reasoning, Quants, Data Interpretation & Verbal. I found the
questions to be of medium difficulty level on an average.
After this round, around 54 students were shortlisted.

Round 2: Group Discussion

We were divided into panels of 10 to 7 people. My panel had all good speakers &
hence no one could be confident about making through this round. Our topic was
"Importance of Media in the society". Since it was an easy topic, all 10 made very
valid points. The GD lasted for 10 mins & each of us got only one chance to speak.
Later all of us were asked to conclude one by one. In the end, 5 of us from my
panel were selected & these were the ones who were articulate, spoke fluently &
did not fumble in between. In this GD, we felt that communication & presentation
skills were given more weightage.
After this round, in all 32 students made it to the next one.

Round 3: Personal Interview + HR

This round, atleast for me, was totally non technical, as I expected. It was the
most smooth interview I ever gave. I started with a brief introduction about
myself & since I had mentioned all my Positions of Responsibility in it, most of my
interview surrounded that. They were specifically intrigued by my position of
Chairperson of the Industry Relations Cell & they asked a lot of questions on what
I learnt from the industry leaders I had invited, what I learnt about the industry,
etc. There were some questions asked on my project too.

The HR then asked me if I had any backlogs, checked if my marks were 60% &
above throughout. Asked which all companies I had applied for previously, etc.
Later they asked me if I had any questions for them.
After this interview, a total of 19 candidates were shortlisted for the final round.

Round 4: Interview with KPMG's Director

My Round 3 round got over at 2:30pm, post which I was expecting a shortlist. We
thought that the last round would just be a check on the culture fit, however, this
round turned out to be the most difficult. It started at 6pm & went on till 10pm. I
was interviewed by the Director, Associate Director & Manager of KPMG. I was
the first one to be interviewed again. The Director asked me about the subjects I
had studied in sem 5 & 6. I named them & after that he started asking me
questions on one of the subjects, CCN. Some questions were actually on topics
that weren't taught to us. I answered what all I could, but for some I did say, "I am
sorry Sir, I am unaware  of this". I honestly felt like the interview had slipped out
of my hand. However, I picked up again once they started asking me questions on
my project & extra curricular activities. The project I had mentioned on my
resume was on Data Analytics so I was asked a few questions on that. Then
looking at the mention of my extra curricular activities in Entrepreneurship, I was
asked why I wanted to join KPMG & not become an Entrepreneur. I was also
asked to mention 3 traits of an Entrepreneur. Post which I was asked some
situational questions that were about  team work & ethics. I was also asked where
I see myself in the next 5 years. This second half of my interview went really well
& I was very well prepared to answer questions based on my resume & situations.
However, a lot of cross questioning took place in this round.
After my round was done, I realized that others were also quizzed on their
subjects as well & most couldn't answer. Some were also asked questions like
explain the mechanism behind the landing of Chandrayan, etc.
A common conclusion we drew from this that they purposely wanted to put us in
uncomfortable situations & check how we still manage to take things forward.
After this round, 7 students were finally selected for this role.

Tips & Facts:

#About KPMG's process:

1. I personally loved how KPMG conducted the whole process not because I got

placed, but because it was extremely fair, giving an equal chance to everyone. Not
to name any other firms, but what a lot of them did was that they conducted
round 1 of the first few people & immediately sent them for subsequent rounds,
while others were still waiting for their first round to start. With KPMG, they let a
round finish for all candidates at once, got into a room, discussed & then gave the
shortlist for the next round. This resulted in them waiting until 11pm in the
college, but they put an effort into giving an equal & fair opportunity to all
candidates. This literally speaks volumes about the ethics of a firm.

2. The harsh truth is that at the end, people who got selected at KPMG were the

once that demonstrated great communication skills & had a strong extra caricular
profile. Their job role eventually also revolves around that. Things like your
branch, CGPA, techstack, etc didn't matter at all. This firm values people skills like
no other.

#About Placements in general:

1. Aptitude Rounds are honestly very luck based. Most people end up not making

through this round unfortunately, even though they fully fit the job role.

2. For GDs, making relevant points is important. However, speaking up & your

communication & articulation matters more. Most people end up staying quiet
because of the pressure, never do that. Try giving personal examples on the topic.
Also remember the difference between GDs & Debates. Be as polite & as humble
as you can.

3. Most interviews are based on your resume & resume alone. Hence do not

mention anything in your resume that you aren't confident about. It's okay if your
resume doesn't have high level projects. But make sure that whichever you are
mentioning, you should be able to explain them & handle questions on them.
Same goes for any PORs/courses etc.

4. Our batch is getting placed at a very weird time. The non tech opportunities we

saw our seniors getting, half of them didn't turn up. Honestly, you shouldn't look
at the previous year's statistics & consider that you will get the same
opportunities. It can be better for your turn (I hope so) or even worse. You can't
predict such things. Look at every opportunity as your last & give your best.

5. Preparation for non tech especially actually starts from your first year itself.

You need to build a profile throughout the 3 years that adds a lot of talking points
in your interview besides your projects & subjects because that is something that
they'll find in every candidate's resume. What they will not find in everyone's
resume are leadership skills, participation in National level competitions, etc.
Being an active participant in things on an around you is very important in my
opinion for non tech profiles atleast.

6. You are reading my interview experience today for KPMG because I was lucky

that the interview went smooth. By this I mean, in most cases, you have same
skills that a certain other candidate also possesses. However, you still don't make
it & other candidate does because he got an easy interviewer who did not grill a
lot while your interview panelist was the opposite & you were asked a lot of tricky
questions that maybe the candidate who got selected also wouldn't know. These
things do happen. It's a lot based on your luck. However, I would recommend you
to also talk to the people who did not get selected to know what went wrong in
their interview so you also know what to avoid, if that thing is in your control.

Prepare as much as you can. Rejections happen, but in the long run, you'll know
that it's for the better good. Godspeed!

1. Aptitude Round

2. Group Discussion

3. Technical + HR Round 1 (Interview with Technical Head + HR manager)

4. Technical + HR Round 2 (Interview with KPMG's Director and Partner)

Round 1: Aptitude Round (55 mins)

The assessment was conducted in online mode on HirePro platform. There were 45 Questions in total which were
split into 15 questions per sections which included Analytical Reasoning, Quantitative, Verbal Ability. There was
no time limit per section. Overall, I found the questions to be of medium difficulty level.
After this round, 54 candidates were shortlisted.
I would recommend the following playlist for the Quantitative aptitude section as many folks find it to be tricky.
Link- https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tnc9ojITRg4&list=PLpyc33gOcbV A4qXMoQ5vmhefTruk5t9lt
There are many questions available on Indiabix for practice. I also referred RS Agarwal book.

Round 2: Group Discussion (2 mins ideation time + 10 mins GD + 1 min to conclude)

We were divided into panels of 8 -10 candidates. My panel had all the good speakers and hence everyone was
skeptical about making through this round. Our topic was "Role of Media in Society". We were given 2 m ins
time for articulating our thoughts so as it was a very common topic I quickly jotted down the points on paper. As
media encompasses a lot of sectors and every individual uses it differently so I kind of mentioned about it. I also
mentioned how media can be regulated so that it doesn't negatively impact the society and also about the positive
side of it. I made sure that I support my points with valid real -life examples and statistics (for eg. I mentioned
about Twitter and how it overcame the issue of fa ke profiles.) As GD is not just about communication, its also
about listening to the fellow panelist s and acknowledging them. After 10 mins of healthy GD, we were given 1
min per panelist to conclude wherein we were expected to of  course give a conclusion and mention whether we
were for or against the particular topic.
After this round, in all 32 students made it to the next round. From my panel 5 candidates were shortlisted.
Few tips from my side:

1. Make sure you participate in mock GDs conducted by the training team of TPO before the placement

season as it will give you an experience and also the realization of your weak points based on the feedback
of the GD evaluator and self-introspection. More you will participate better you will get at it. As reading
books and communication was an integral part of my day-to-day life and my experience of heading couple
of student organizations parallelly helped to ace this round.

2. In GD, communication skills definitely matter no doubts but it should be backed with valid points and

wholesome perspective on the given topic. If you have less understanding about the topic so just maintain
your calm and listen to few points of your panelists and try to come up with something rather by staying
quiet.

3. Most of the folks just focus on putting their points but not on listening and maintaining a positive body

language and they incur demerits. Most of the time you will be listening and just don't get into a debate.
Be polite and maintain the decorum.

4. If you have any doubts related to the given topic, make sure you ask the evaluator regarding the same and

then start off with ideation.

Round 3: Technical + HR Round 1 (20 mins approx)

This round was completely resume based. They asked me to give a brief introduction about myself after which I
was asked to explain my projects one by one. I made sure that I maintain a proper flow while explaining my
projects. The flow is as follows:

• Introduction + Motivation behind the specific project

• Need and practical implementation

• Explanation of the tech stack used with proper reasoning. (I prefer to use pen and paper in order explain

the project with the help of block diagrams, ER diagrams wherever required.)

• Explanation of the output in great detail by mentioning all the features and functions.

• Any additional features you can add to improvise the project basically the future scope.

Interviewer seemed impressed by the explanation but he did ask me some follow up questions in between my
explanation. He was more oriented towards cloud computing. He asked me basic  questions related to AWS and
also the pandas as well as pytesseract library of python which I used for OCR. He then took interest in data
visualization and asked me about how did I go about making dashboards and further he gave me some random
real-life situations and asked me to provide the technical implementation details with overall time frames. As two
of my projects revolved around data engineering it definitely gave me a slight edge I feel.
After this the HR person stepped in and she asked me to she d some light on my contributions in TPO and
Entrepreneurship Cell. As I was parallelly heading three student bodies so she  also asked about my motivation
behind being this active and taking various initiatives in the college and also  couple of questions on  time
management. She also asked me on why did I apply for this role? Couple of questions on KPMG and this marked
the end of the interview. I knew that I had aced this round as well.
After this round, around 19 candidates made it to the next round.

Round 4: Technical + HR round 2 (1-hour approx)

This round was taken by the director and partner of KPMG. This was unlike the standard HR round where  I
wasn't asked very basic and standard questions  but they focused more upon my exposure towards business and
entrepreneurship and whether I could deploy and use my technical as well soft skills in order to cater the client's
requirements. They started off with appreciating my overall resume, they asked me that why am I not starting up
my own venture considering the kind of network  and relevant exposure in entrepreneurship  that I had . They
conveyed that they were 99% convinced that I would drop this offer for my future startup  and my task was to
convince them that I won't do that. So, I mentioned about our placement policy, SPTBI as well as how I can use
my entrepreneurial mindset and business exposure for KPMG. After few exchanges on the similar lines, they
moved on to cloud and gave me a situation where a client wants to use AWS but wants to spend minimal amount
on it, so which services will be my recommendation  followed by an explanation of the entire architecture using
those services with an estimate amount for the entire setup.  There was also a question on why  AWS is the most
preferred cloud in India?  After this they asked me whether I had some plans for higher education and if no then
what's the reason? Obviously, considering the shorter picture I said no and I gave them couple of genuine reasons
to support my decision. But I conveyed that if KPMG gives me an opportunity for higher study, I will definitely
consider and if not then I will prefer distance learning courses over an offline degree  if my future role demands
management expertise. Prepare well for such standard questions beforehand.
Refer this link for standard HR Questions with answers which I had prepared -
https://drive.google.com/file/d/1ukWKckgkcs99Ww5S5OI9diirGgHwgP9e/view?usp=sharing
They asked me about New Education Policy and how it can be improvised and put in action. As I prefer to stay
updated with current affairs so this was something I had red  before and given a thought upon so I explained the
policy and my thought process and they were satisfied with it. Then they were open for questions? So, I asked
them about the overall internship structure for us and few  questions on the  different roles and opportunities  as
well.
Finally, 7 candidates were selected for an I+P opportunity at KPMG.

Few points about placements in general:

1. Honestly, the first round is pretty random for all companies as a lot of folks end up solving all the questions

but only a few fortunate ones end up getting shortlisted. So, if you aren't able to clear the first round
definitely keep practicing but don't get demotivated as eventually you will end up getting shortlisted but
till then make sure you are covered with all the topics and equipped with relevant skills in your arsenal.

2. I always focused on overall development and was never biased towards anything . Through my projects

and by solving dsa problems I had gained the necessary technical skills  as well as aptitude  and my
leadership experience came through my positions of responsibilities. I would encourage you guys to also
focus on these two aspects and take part in national level competitions  beforehand, be a part of some
student body which will make your profile wholesome. I had seen that there are lot of folks having
redundant profiles, you got to bring something new to the table. Especially a firm like KPMG expects you
to have that differentiating mindset.

3. Embrace failures and remember that these experiences are  just making you intellect ually as well as

mentally strong for the new chapter of your life that lies ahead of placements. Placement season definitely
made me mentally strong and at the same time it boosted my confidence and made me a lot humbler as
well. You will also notice many positive shifts in your personality. Trust the process, give your best.

I would like to end by highlighting this verse -
He who is satisfied with gain which comes of its own accord, who is free from duality and does not envy, who
is steady in both success and failure, is never entangled, although performing actions.

journey.prep:
• Practice DSA regularly

• Have a good knowledge of OOPS, DBMS, SQL and any of the following languages (Java, Python,

C++). I would prefer Java, since most of companies require java but its not compulsory

• I haven't heard anyone being asked concepts of OS and CCN much. For these 2 subjects some

standard questions are enough

• For aptitude questions, puzzles prepare from Indiabix, GFG. That's sufficient

• Prepare a nice introduction for yourself and practice it. If you give a nice introduction that sets a nice

tone for the rest of interview

• Know your resume very well, especially projects you mentioned. Take help of your friends or gpt

and prepare as many questions as possible that you could be asked in your interview and prepare
accordingly. Also prepare some introduction ready for each project whenever asked to give an
overview of the project. Introduction should be just 5-6 lines regarding your project like why did you
do it? What it is? What are the features? And finally the tech stack. Keep the answers as simple as
simple. If you use big words in your answers and you don't have an idea about them then the
interviewer can cross question it, so keep the answer simple so he also understands it easily.

• Whenever asked any question if you know then answer it in the easiest way possible. If you don't

know any answer then tell it honestly, or if you know it slightly then tell how much you know. Don't
be quiet. Don't give answers in just one word. If you are asked a certain concept, then it's better to
explain it with an example, this shows the interviewer you haven't only mugged the answer but you
genuinely know it.

• If you are asked a DSA question then discuss your approach with the interviewer, don't stay quiet.

Let the interviewer know how you come up with the solution. They are more interested in how you
think rather than the answer. And if possible first give a brute force solution and then optimize it
further.

• Be relaxed in your interview. Most of the interviewers are friendly and help you. Ask questions

whenever you are stuck. Prepare some questions that you will ask the interviewer at the end of the
interview.

• Do a background check of the company before going into the interview. Generally the companies

values, what it does, what are it's some popular products/services, any recent achievement/news
regarding that company

• And lastly, don't worry too much about the result. Focus more on preparation. This is only a start of a

new phase in life, you have an entire race ahead of yourself. Even if you are rejected in any
--- PAGE 6 ---
interview, don't get frustrated. Go home, eat dinner, do something relaxing and take a good sleep.
Instead of whining about why I didn't get selected, focus on what went wrong and try to improve
that next time. This was my 6th interview, so let me tell you the placement process is very tiring and
stressful. But don't give up hope, there's no point in that because companies will keep coming. Our
TPO is doing a pretty good job, compared to other colleges.

• And luck does play an important role in the process to be honest, sometimes you see people less

capable than you get selected, but luck isn't in our hands, what is, is hard work. So focus on
preparation. Learn from your mistakes instead of being sad and look forward.

• Maintain a positive demeanor and always wear a smile. Project confidence in your responses, even

when addressing incorrect answers.
References:
DSA - Striver SDE Sheet, Coding-Decoded SDE sheet, Love Babbar SDE sheet. Any one of them you can
follow
DBMS, OOPS - GFG, Javatpoint, Interviewbit are sufficient. Search for top 50 interview questions and
prepare accordingly
SQL - For theory you can refer to GFG, javatpoint. For practicing queries I would suggest hackerrank.
Mostly focus of joins, group by, sub-query, limit
OS, CCN - some some standard questions from GFG
Puzzles - Indiabix, GFG
Wishing you all the best for your placements and for your future, everyone!

Round 1: Online Assessment (6/08/2023)

test. Everyone who had registered was eligible to take the test. Test login credentials were sent via mail to

3. Help the Rook

Problem Statement: You have a chessboard (8x8), with few of the cells marked as taken (X).
You have a rook that can only move in straight lines: horizontal or vertical but cannot cross any cell that is
taken (marked X).
You start at a position S and need to end at position E. You can assume that there is always a route from
S to E.
--- PAGE 2 ---
Task is to find the minimum number of steps the rook needs to take to get from position S to position E on
the board.
Eg.
S
E
Grid is assumed to start at (0,0) top left corner to (77) bottom right corner.
The sample above is represented with the following inputs to the function below
taken = [[1,0], [1,1], [1,2], [1,3]]
start = [0,0]
end = [2,0]
For the sample above the solution is 3
Step 1 (0,0) (0,4)
Step 2 (0,4) -> (2,4)
Step 3 (2,4) > (2,0)
Note: You only need to implement the given function. Do not read input, instead use the arguments to the
function. Do not use any inbuilt method else solution will be considered as invalid

4. Simple Unix-like Change Directory Simulator (I don't remember the exact question but it was

similar to this
Problem Statement: You are tasked with implementing a simplified version of the Unix "cd" (change
directory) command simulator. The goal is to create a function that takes a current directory path and a
directory change command, and returns the resulting directory path after applying the change.

2. Longest Perfect Subsequence

Problem Statement: Calculate the length of the longest "perfect subsequence" from a given string s. A
perfect subsequence is a sequence of characters from the input string where the difference between the
indices of any two characters is at most k.
--- PAGE 3 ---
Input:
k (integer): An integer representing the maximum allowed difference between indices of characters in the
perfect subsequence.
s (string): A string containing lowercase English letters.
Output:
Returns an integer representing the length of the longest perfect subsequence in the input string s.
E.g.
int k=2;
String s = "abjbka";
// The longest perfect subsequence is "abcbda" with indices [0, 1, 3, 5], which has a length of 4.
// Therefore, the result should be 4.

f. Find Complexity
g. Find What is Error
h. File Management in Python
I was able to solve all the coding questions and most mcqs. There was no negative marking so I attempted
all the questions
**Around 30 candidates were selected for interviews (3 candidates were selected for both roles and rest
were selected for only 1 role, though in the end it didn't matter for which role you were selected, depending
on how you performed in the interview you were selected for a role)

Round 2: Technical Interview-1

For most candidates, the duration of the round was 40-60 minutes.
There was no fixed pattern of questions asked in the interview. Some were asked about the projects in their
resume while some were asked coding questions or sal queries, or totally out of box questions
--- PAGE 4 ---
Let me share my experience:
My interviewer's name was Priyam Sinha. So first I was asked to introduce myself. Then he asked me to
explain one of the projects which was a fitness website. Then since my other 2 projects were related to
machine learning he asked me whether I am more focused on ML, to which I answered that's not the case
and I am still exploring various domains and am currently planning to work on cloud computing for my
final year project. We discussed it for around 5 mins then he asked me questions related to Heap Data
Structure like what is heap, what does it work, what are its uses, what are its types etc. they were general
questions and i answered most of them correctly. Then he moved on to dsa. I was asked 2 questions on dsa:

1. https://leetcode.com/problems/amount-of-time-for-binary-tree-to-be-infected/description/

2. https://leetcode.com/problems/search-in-rotated-sorted-array/

For the first question I was asked to write the pseudo code and then was told to dry run the code with an
example. I was also asked to tell the time and space complexity for the program.
For the second question the required time complexity by the interviewer was O(log(n)). I was only told to
explain the approach and write the if-else conditions required in the program.
This was it. He asked whether I had any questions to which I asked about his role and what companies he
has worked with prior to IDfy (I searched about him on LinkedIn, so I framed my questions accordingly)
Around 9 students were short-listed for the next round.

Round 3: Technical Interview-2

For most candidates, the duration of the round is 60-70 minutes.
Again this round was a technical round(there were no HR rounds for this company). Interviewers were
basically swapped. The interviewer asks whether this question was asked to you in first interview(*answer
honestly since they have a report of the previous round.
Let me share my experience:
This time my interviewer's name was Niranjan. He first asked me what questions were asked to me in my
last interview. Then he gave me 2 standard puzzles:

1. https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/puzzle-1-how-to-measure-45-minutes-using-two-identical-wires/

2. https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/puzzle-farmer-goat-wolf-cabbage/

Then he moved on to my resume and since there were projects related to machine learning, he asked me
questions related to CNN(convolutional neural network) which is a type of deep neural network. Questions
were what do you mean by convolution in CNN, how is it different from other neural networks,what are
feature maps. I actually didn't have a very good idea of what it was, but I said what I knew. There was a
mention of numpy and open cv libraries in my project so he wrote a code and asked me what the output
would be. I didn't know about it so I answered honestly and said I don't know and for the projects I referred
to different documents and research papers and did accordingly so never actually learned python. (To be
honest at this point in my interview I thought I wasn't going to get selected). Then he asked me to write a
--- PAGE 5 ---
code for a lift/elevator (you heard right a **lift**). He first asked about what will be the inputs, then after
discussing what will the inputs he told to write the code. At this point my mind was going crazy but still I
wrote some code. Then he gave me different scenarios/edge-cases and asked me to think how will you solve
it. I thought and suggested my methods to which he countered everytime with a different edge-case.
Basically the point of this question was to test my thinking skill. Then he told me to write the code for this
question we would require 2 writing board and that he also can't write the code. Then he asked me how to
measure how much it had rained in mumbai on any particular day. We discussed this for some minutes and I
wasn't able to answer this properly. Then he asked me some mcqs that were there in the test and asked me to
write the code for one of the questions. Then he told me to write a pseudo code of implementation of a stack
using 2 queues and dry run it. I wrote both the codes properly. This was the last question of the interview.
To be honest after how this interview went I wasn't thinking I would get selected but the results were
declared and 6 students were shortlisted for the job (3 for each role) and I was one of them

customSections.title: Advice & Tips for Juniors
customSections.content:
• Practice DSA regularly

• Have a good knowledge of OOPS, DBMS, SQL and any of the following languages (Java, Python,

C++). I would prefer Java, since most of companies require java but its not compulsory

• I haven't heard anyone being asked concepts of OS and CCN much. For these 2 subjects some

standard questions are enough

• For aptitude questions, puzzles prepare from Indiabix, GFG. That's sufficient

• Prepare a nice introduction for yourself and practice it. If you give a nice introduction that sets a nice

tone for the rest of interview

• Know your resume very well, especially projects you mentioned. Take help of your friends or gpt

and prepare as many questions as possible that you could be asked in your interview and prepare
accordingly. Also prepare some introduction ready for each project whenever asked to give an
overview of the project. Introduction should be just 5-6 lines regarding your project like why did you
do it? What it is? What are the features? And finally the tech stack. Keep the answers as simple as
simple. If you use big words in your answers and you don't have an idea about them then the
interviewer can cross question it, so keep the answer simple so he also understands it easily.

• Whenever asked any question if you know then answer it in the easiest way possible. If you don't

know any answer then tell it honestly, or if you know it slightly then tell how much you know. Don't
be quiet. Don't give answers in just one word. If you are asked a certain concept, then it's better to
explain it with an example, this shows the interviewer you haven't only mugged the answer but you
genuinely know it.

• If you are asked a DSA question then discuss your approach with the interviewer, don't stay quiet.

Let the interviewer know how you come up with the solution. They are more interested in how you
think rather than the answer. And if possible first give a brute force solution and then optimize it
further.

• Be relaxed in your interview. Most of the interviewers are friendly and help you. Ask questions

whenever you are stuck. Prepare some questions that you will ask the interviewer at the end of the
interview.

• Do a background check of the company before going into the interview. Generally the companies

values, what it does, what are it's some popular products/services, any recent achievement/news
regarding that company

• And lastly, don't worry too much about the result. Focus more on preparation. This is only a start of a

new phase in life, you have an entire race ahead of yourself. Even if you are rejected in any
--- PAGE 6 ---
interview, don't get frustrated. Go home, eat dinner, do something relaxing and take a good sleep.
Instead of whining about why I didn't get selected, focus on what went wrong and try to improve
that next time. This was my 6th interview, so let me tell you the placement process is very tiring and
stressful. But don't give up hope, there's no point in that because companies will keep coming. Our
TPO is doing a pretty good job, compared to other colleges.

• And luck does play an important role in the process to be honest, sometimes you see people less

capable than you get selected, but luck isn't in our hands, what is, is hard work. So focus on
preparation. Learn from your mistakes instead of being sad and look forward.

• Maintain a positive demeanor and always wear a smile. Project confidence in your responses, even

when addressing incorrect answers.
References:
DSA - Striver

journey.howSecured:
After being the only one rejected by Deutsche Bank and in the last round of MSCI and 11 other
companies, EDS visited us on the 17th of August.
There were a total of 5 rounds. PPT and the first two rounds were conducted on the same day in online
mode, while the other rounds were conducted in offline mode. Students were not allowed to apply for both
Data and SDE roles; only the first round was common for both.
All the students who applied appeared for the test.

1. Aptitude Round - 17 August 2023, 7:00 PM

This round was held online and was entirely based on aptitude. Practicing Indiabix questions will help you
pass this round.
This round was approximately 45 minutes to 1 hour long.
Around 70 students applied for the SDE role, but only 25 qualified for the next round.

2. Coding Round - 17 August 2023, 8:30 PM

For this round, there were two sections. The first section had coding questions, and the second had
SQL-related questions. The coding questions were easy to medium-level LeetCode questions.
This round was approximately 45 minutes to 1 hour long.
Only 15 students qualified for the next round.
--- PAGE 2 ---

3. Technical Round 1 - 22 August 2023, 2:00 PM

Interviewed by the EDS Technical Lead of the Web Department
In this round, we had to give interviews in pairs, and both of us had to give answers to the same questions.
Based on your answers, you will be evaluated.
Interviewers will decide with whom you will be paired. It is based on your resume and the similar interests
mentioned in it.
The interview started with our introduction. There were 2 interviewers; they provided us with a sheet of
paper and asked us the following questions one by one, the same for both and at the same time:

1. A very simple question about an array

2. How to center a div?

3. Create a JSON from an object

4. Convert the above JSON and store it

5. An SQL join query

The questions were relatively easy, and I was able to answer all the questions. For question 4, I asked them
if I could modify JSON so it could be efficiently stored. They allowed me to modify it.
For the final question, they were not satisfied with both of our answers, as they needed an efficient query.
This round lasted for 1 to 1.5 hours.
At the end, I asked him a question. "Suppose a framework that is being used in one of your projects gets
deprecated and is no longer supported. How do you handle this situation?" To which he answered, we use
Dockers, and in that Docker we can keep the framework of any version, and it will continue to work until we
change or remove it ourselves. I was a little confused with the answer, but he was right: the framework will
continue to be used as long as it is inside the docker and is unchanged.
Only 7 students qualified for the next round.

4. Techno-HR Round 1 - 22 August 2023, 6:00 PM

Interviewed by the EDS co-founder, CEO, and CTO
My interview was really late, and it was conducted online via Zoom call. The interview started with my
introduction, then he went through my resume and asked me a few questions based on my projects. Then we
discussed some of our experience working on different technologies, as I worked on both Android and the
Web. He asked me a question related to SQL, and I was able to give an answer. He then asked me if I was
comfortable working on React Native, as previously I built apps with Flutter and Java but not with React
Native. I said it would be fine. I will get the opportunity to add another skill to my knowledge set. It was a
friendly conversation.
This round lasted for about 1 to 1.5 hours.
At the end, I asked him a question. "Consider a framework that you are currently using, let's say React
Native. You mentioned that you use it for your application, but we also have Flutter. Let's say in the future,
Flutter or any other framework gives 2x performance compared to React Native. In that case, will you
switch your framework? This will also include the fact that current employees will have to learn the new
technology and the time required to migrate or rewrite the entire codebase in a new language or framework.
How will you handle this?" He answered to this question by saying that if the new framework gives us 2x
performance, then we will definitely switch to it. The performance of an application matters the most, and
we want to deliver the best performance to our users. I was satisfied with the answer.
--- PAGE 3 ---
Only 1 student qualified for the final round.

5. Techno-HR Round 11 - 22 August 2023, 7:30 PM

Interviewed by the EDS Chief Architect
While waiting for the result, I was surprised to know that there would be another HR round that I had to
face. After getting rejected in the HR rounds again and again, I knew this was my final test.
This interview was also conducted online via Zoom call. Again, the interview started with my introduction,
and we discussed some of my projects and started talking about the new technologies. The interviewer was
very chill.
This round lasted for about half an hour.
At the end, I asked him a question. Honestly, I do not remember what I asked.
After about an hour, they announced the result, and finally I got selected :)
Some Tips:
After getting rejected again and again because of my lack of communication skills and preparing again and
again, this interview was very easy for me.

• Make sure that you have good communication skills; if not, practice more and more.

• Solve Indiabix questions; do not take the aptitude test lightly, as I did, and it cost me 3 companies.

• Practice Leetcode questions daily, and the technical interviews will be very easy for you.

• It is up to you to ask questions at the end; do not ask too many questions.

• Always go through the company's website before the interview.

Feel free to ask me any doubts on my LinkedIn account.
All the best for your placements :)
And of course, you must not give up!

panelists are keen on evaluating your authenticity and eagerness to learn. During the interview, it was

1. Online Test [ 96 candidates appeared for this round]

On 10th August, we had Pre-Placement Talk at 12pm followed by an Online Test at 2:30pm.
Quick Tip (For all Companies) : Be Active and Vocal during Pre Placement Talk, answer to the questions
given by them + ask them questions. This shows you are interested in the company and the HR
manager will notice you and it would be highly beneficial in your HR Round (TRUST ME)
The Online Test was conducted on SHL Platform. We had to give this test on our laptop in Offline Mode.
The test was 1 hour 30 mins long.
Test Consisted of 4 parts.
1] Verbal Ability -12 questions-Moderate difficulty
2] Quantitative Aptitude- 12 Questions- Easy to Moderate
3] Logical Reasoning - 12 Questions- Easy
4] Coding - 2 Questions
For first 3 sections, questions were easy-moderate level but time was a concern since each section had to be
completed in 12 mins. So this section mainly tests your speed in calculating answers.
For preparing Aptitude questions for all companies, refer to this youtube channel namediCareerRide'
https://youtube.com/playlist?list=PLpyc33gOcbVA4qXMoQ5vmhefTrukSt9lt
Make sure you start preparing for aptitude questions 2-3 months before the interview process. Don't take
this lightly since maximum companies take these test to eliminate most of the candidates.
Visit indiabix. com to practice these questions.
--- PAGE 2 ---
For Coding, time given was 50 mins. Questions were very easy.
1st question was based on Prime numbers.
2nd question was based on searching of char in a string and return its count.
Out of 96 candidates, 35 were shortlisted for Interview Rounds the next day.

2. Technical Interview Round [35 candidates appeared for this round]

Technical Interview started at 10:00am
There were 3 panels each containing 2 panelists. So at a time 3 interviews were taking place.
My first question was "Introduce yourself". Then they asked me extensively about my Projects.
NOTE: Make sure you know each and every word of your Resume. Most of the Tech interview rounds are
resume based. So make sure you prepare well.
After that, they asked me my preferred programming language and gave me a problem to solve. The
question was To count Frequency of numbers in an array". I had to write a Pseudocode on paper. Make sure
you speak with the interviewer while solving question. By communicating with them, they will understand
your approach. 2nd question asked was based on dynamic programming. (longest increasing subsequence)
To solve coding question, first give them a brute force approach, then optimize it and explain it to them.
In of my projects, i used MySQL database. So they asked me to draw the databases used in my project and
based on that databases, they asked me 2-3 SQL queries to solve on paper. The queries were difficult and
needed some thinking. (queries were based on JOINS, GROUP BY clause)
I had used Java in one of my projects. So they asked me "which version of Java you used and Why?'
I had used Java Swing toolkit in one of my projects. First 10 minutes of interview was on Java Swing toolkit
itself. The interviewer asked extensively about it.
Then he asked me "What you know about TransUnion" and "What is CIBIL Score'. (CIBIL is owned and
operated by Transunion).
At the end, they asked me my Preferred work location. Interview lasted for around 20-25 mins.
NOTE: Each panel asked different questions. Some candidates were asked extensively on DSA while
some were asked on Resume. So prepare accordingly.
Out of 35 candidates, 15 got shortlisted for HR Interview.

3. HR Round [15 candidates appeared for this round]

HR round started at around 2:30pm after lunch break.
--- PAGE 3 ---
There were 3 panelists. First they asked me to "Introduce Myself". Then 'your Long term career goals',
'preferred tech stack to work upon', Things i learned from courses & projects done by me'. This
interview lasted for around 15 mins.
Tip: Be real, Be yourself and answer the questions confidently.
10 candidates (including me) were selected for the job.

journey.howSecured:
1. Aptitude Test

2. Pre - Placement Talk

3. Interview Rounds

a. Technical Round 1
b. Technical Round 2 + HR

1. Aptitude Test [229 students (174 BTech + 55 MCA) appeared for this round]

This was an online aptitude test conducted on MeritTrac's Online Assessment Engine -
PARIKSHA. The test consisted of 60 questions, with 20 questions each in the verbal, analytical,
and quantitative sections, with no negative marking. The time limit was 60 minutes so timing is
the key here. There was a cutoff for this test which was not known to us.
38 students were shortlisted for the next round.

2. Pre-Placement Talk

This round started at 10 am. We were briefed about the company, including its values, various
programs, and significant milestones. In the end, we were given the opportunity to ask
questions. Make sure to ask questions (good ones) to get noticed. I had made a question in two
parts which I had thought to ask one in PPT and other part in Interviews. Question Was "Could
you please elaborate on the specific security measures and protocols that Nomura has in place
to safeguard client data and financial transactionsạ
--- PAGE 2 ---

3. Technical Round 1(30 - 35 minutes)

During my interview at around 11:50 am, I began by introducing myself and expressing Bill
Gates as my role model, citing his entrepreneurial spirit and philanthropy as my inspiration. The
interviewer then thoroughly reviewed my resume and engaged in discussions about my
projects, particularly focusing on the technologies used. Notably, in one project utilizing
DynamoDB, he inquired about the choice over SQL and MongoDB. My passion for the projects
led him to ask why I hadn't considered open-sourcing one of them. He showed interest in the
details of all my projects, even asking if there was a working model. Additionally, he inquired
about a non-tech internship had completed.
To test my knowledge and interest in the company, he asked what I knew about Nomura. I used
the opportunity to inquire about the company's security measures, continuing a question I had
posed during the pre-placement talk. The interviewer concluded by providing positive feedback,
considering me a strong candidate with creative potential.
15 students got shortlisted for the next round, and 13 were waitlisted. The waitlisted candidates
were called for an additional review round out of which 3 students moved to the final round (not
sure what was asked in the review round). Finally, 18 students moved to the final round.

3. Technical Round 2 + HR (45 - 50 minutes)

My interview was scheduled to be two separate rounds, an HR round, and a technical round.
However, due to time constraints, the two rounds were merged into a single round, which
started around 4 pm. The panel consisted of two members, one from the HR team and another
from the Tech team.
The interview commenced with questions about my proficiency in programming languages. I
mentioned SQL and Python. They presented a simple SQL task where I had to count the total
number of males and females in a given column (Gender). Though initially nervous, I explained
a more complex approach using multiple select statements and Union. With their helpful hint
about using the GROUP BY function, I quickly grasped the simpler solution.
The technical questions continued, focusing on SQL. They asked me to write a query to replace
male with female and vice versa. Later, they inquired about joins and window functions, and the
discussion went on to my projects, which seemed to captivate their interest. We spent around
half an hour discussing my projects in detail.
The panel then challenged me with some puzzles to solve, followed by questions about my
tech-related learning beyond the college curriculum. They specifically asked about Blockchain
and whether I had worked on any projects related to it. The conversation then transitioned to HR
--- PAGE 3 ---
questions, including why I chose Nomura, why they should select me, a time when I performed
at my best, and how I would handle a team.
The entire interview lasted about an hour, providing a comprehensive evaluation of my technical

For the placement process, a total of 3 rounds were conducted. 1 MCQ round and 2 walk-in interviews were organized.

1. Round 1:  Online MCQ Test

Approximately 170 students from B.Tech and 55 students from MCA appeared for the test. The test was based on Verbal, Quantitative and analytical reasoning. 60 questions (20 from each section ) were to be attempted in a time frame of 60 minutes. The marks of this round weren't revealed. I think I got most of the Verbal and analytical problems correct and was left out with some 6-7 questions of Quantitative section. The problems were similar to those which come in competitive exams like NTSE. I would suggest trying to complete the verbal section as fast as possible as quantitative questions take up more time than others. 27 students from B.Tech and 11 from MCA made it to the interviews and I was one of them.

2. Round 2: Interview-1

Following the pre-placement talk, the interviews for the shortlisted students were scheduled within the college campus. The VP of the company ( who also presented the pre-placement talk ) was my interviewer for the first round. With a formal exchange of greetings, the interviewer asked for my resume and asked me to introduce myself as he went through my resume. After I properly introduced myself, I was asked some questions on one of my projects like a rough data flow of my project, why did I choose the problem statement etc. He then suggested an extension to my project and asked my views upon how I would implement it. He then out of the blue asked me to write any piece of code of python on paper and asked me to explain it to him. I used one of my functions that was used in my project. After this , he asked me to write the logic of a calendar application without using existing libraries from where I could directly import the interface. To this I answered by mapping the starting day( this can be calculated by odd days) to the number and using % operator to achieve a cyclicity of 7 days while keeping in mind the edge cases like a leap year, 30\31 days of a month etc. The interviewer seemed quite satisfied with my approach. He then asked me about a time when I had to balance multiple priorities at once to which I answered relevently. At the end he asked me 2 puzzles, one of them was an easy variation of Tower of Hanoi and a Water Jug problem. I was able to answer the first one quickly but the second one was a bit difficult for me as there were 3 jugs and no wastage of water was allowed. The problem was that we have 3 containers of capacity 10L, 6L, and 7L out of which 10L one was empty and the other were filled. Without wasting water or external supply we had to measure 9L. I started to solve it and while solving i was discussing my approach with the interviewer. He told me that I was on the right track but after a couple of minutes of solving the problem, I was stopped due to time constraints. He then asked me if I had questions for him and I asked him the questions that I had in my mind.
All in all this round was majorly focused about how I approach problems and my ideation. However, asking other students, their experiences were different, some were asked OOPS, SQL and named algorithms too. So it totally depended upon the interviewer.
11 People from B.Tech and 3 or 4 MCA were selected for the next round . However there was a review round also where 8 Btech and 5 MCA students were given another chance to again get interviewed and get selected for the next round. This took place maybe because the company was not sure whether to select these students for the next round. A total of 3 students made it to the next round from the review round.

3. Round 3: Interview-2

This interview had 2 panelists. After handing over my resume, I was asked to give my introduction. One of the interviewers was quite impressed with one of the projects saying that the problem statement was very unique. The interviewers carefully went through everything on the resume and asked every little detail of each project to which I answered best to my knowledge. The interview went pretty smooth as I answered pretty much everything confidently. One of the panelists said that he did not want to ask any tech questions to me as most of my projects were front end extensive and maybe the interviewers had a command over SQL, so I guess that's the reason I wasn't asked one. 11 students were finally selected for the programme.

1. Aptitude Test

2. Pre - Placement Talk

3. Interview Rounds

a. Technical Round 1
b. Technical Round 2 + HR

1.     Aptitude Test  [229 students (174 BTech + 55 MCA) appeared for this round]

This was an online aptitude test conducted on MeritTrac's Online Assessment Engine - PARIKSHA. The test
comprised of 60 questions, with 20 questions each in the verbal, analytical, and quantitative sections, with no
negative marking. The time limit was  60 minutes so timing is the key here. There was a cutoff for this test
which was not known to us.
38 students were shortlisted for the next round.

2. Pre-Placement Talk

This round was supposed to start at 9:30 am , but due to some delay it  got deferred to around 10 am. We
were briefed about the company,  including its values, various programs, and significant milestones. In the
end, we were given the opportunity to ask questions. Make sure to ask questions (good ones) to get noticed.

3. Technical Round 1 (30 - 35 minutes)

My interview was scheduled at 10:30 am, but again it got delayed and began around 11 am. This round
was entirely resume based. The interviewer  did not ask for my intro and directly started by asking my
branch and whether we had any CS related subjects in our curriculum to which I replied that we had them
in our open electives/minor course in CS which I had pursued. Then, he asked me about the extra-curricular
activities section in my resume, what I did during my volunteering experience etc. Then he came to the

projects section, and asked me in -depth questions about one of my projects, which was essentially a
desktop-based application using Java and MySQL. He gave me a pen and paper and told me to draw a
basic UI of the entire process to check my basic understanding of the project. Then he asked me some
situation-based questions on my project like how would your app handle the situation if the user tries to
write special characters in the name section. After that, he gave me some workplace -based situations,
which were: what if your manager tells you to work on a particular topic, and he asks your colleague to
work on the same topic too, h ow would you approach this situation. The second question was, what if
there is a particular topic on which your idea clashes with your manager's idea, what would you do in this
case. These questions were basically to check my collaboration skills and how well I can work with others.
In the end, he asked me if I had questions for him to which I asked him 2 questions. I wasn't asked any
tech questions in this round, but few others were asked some questions on data structures, SQL, puzzles
etc, it depends from panelist to panelist (there were about 10 of them).

15 students got shortlisted for the next round, and 13 were waitlisted.  The waitlisted candidates were
called for an additional review round out of which 3 students moved to the final round (not sure what was
asked in the review round). Finally, 18 students moved to the final round.

3. Technical Round 2 + HR ( 45 - 50 minutes)

Ideally there was supposed to be a separate HR round, but due to the time crunch, it was merged into 1
single round. My turn came at around 3 pm. This time, I was being interviewed by a panel of 3 including
the Vice President, and 1 member each from the HR and Tech teams. The interview began by a basic "Tell
me about yourself" question. Be careful of what you mention in your int ro as questions are asked on the
basis of that. Then the interviewer asked me some in-depth questions on SQL AND DBMS like what it is,
What are analytical functions, write an SQL query to print the salaries whose frequency is >5 in the
database and whether a group by clause would be relevant in this case. Then he drew a table on a paper
and asked me the output if right outer join or inner join was applied.  After that, he asked me about the
various ways to delete( drop, truncate, delete ), their definition, which is faster, and whether we can "undo"
the truncate command.
After that he came to the projects section, surprisingly the panel started asking about one of the electronics
project which I had mentioned  (I wasn't expecting it) , they wanted to know the b asic overview, our
approach, and since I had mentioned that we were filing a patent for our project, they were curious to know
the entire process, the novelty, whether any such product was already present in the market, future scope,
etc. Then, I was asked again about the Java project, about the techstack and database used, where is OOPS
being implemented in my code,  and then they asked me to explain a bit about what was going on in the
backend, and 1 situation-based question. He asked me whether this project would work on Linux, to which
I replied yes as Java is a platform -independent language. He then asked the reason behind it, I told him
that it is because of JVM, then he asked me to draw a diagram showing the relationship between the 3
components of th e Java architec ture.  After that, he asked me my approach to a basic data structures
problem(https://leetcode.com/problems/valid-anagram/description/) .
In the end, I was asked a HR question as to why I want to work with Nomura. After that, the VP asked me
if I had any questions for him to which I asked him a question and a follow -up question based on his
answer.

I was able to answer almost all of the questions, but I was unsure whether I would get selected or not as it
was my first offline interview. Finally, the results were announced at 6 pm, and 11 students (10 B Tech +
1 MCA) were selected and I was one of them.

query consisting of a set of employees (eg: for say 10 employees, a query can be
(1,4,6,7,9)). We have to find the minimum of, for all nodes in the set farthest distance(d)
from that node to the other nodes in the set. Let's say the distance of other nodes from 1 is
[0,2,3,4,3], so the farthest node is at a distance of 4 from 1. Similarly we obtain the
farthest distances(d) from other nodes and we have to return the minimum of that. Tried
solving it using brute force using BFS but was facing some problems with the input.

4. I  don't  remember  this  question  at  all  as  I  hardly  spent  30s  on  it.  It  was  something  related

Question 1  : Given N projects with cost,profit. Select  k projects which will yield the maximum
profit. Also, after completion of each project the profit adds up to the initial wealth(0 at start).
Started with N^2logN approach first which included sorting based on cost and iterating over all
projects having cost <= current wealth and selecting the maximum profit one. Optimized it using
a heap to NlogN+NlogN.
Question 2:  Given 2 strings we have to make maximum  non-overlapping lines connecting equal
characters. It was based on the idea of LCS, solved it recursively first and then optimized it using
DP.

minimum jump length(d) to reach the end of the string. If you land on  'L'  you go left by 1 and if

stage. I gave an approach to divide the problem into subproblems which involved from a given
'R' reaching the next 'R' which would eventually ensure we cover the entire string. The
maximum distance between two consecutive 'R's would be the minimum jump distance that

cases  will  decide  if  you'll  advance  into  the  next  round  or  not.  They  asked  me  to  make  a  recursion
tree for the same and save the dp states in a table/dict too.
The interviewers were quite friendly and in the end I asked a few questions.

Tips  :  Be  confident.  Make  sure  you  are  able  to  explain  your  approach  clearly.  Keep  writing  your

-  What data will you store?

-  What will you use to store that data?

-  How will you contact the delivery agents?

1. PhonePe interviews are mostly DSA based so make sure to focus more on that. Study the working

and time complexities of all important data structures and algorithms.

2. During the technical interview, make sure to think out loud. It is important that you communicate

your ideas and approaches to the interviewer, since they are interested in your thought process and
logic building. If they know what direction you are thinking in, they can also provide appropriate
hints.

3. When given a dsa question, firstly explain your own understanding of the problem so the interviewer

can make sure you have got it right and also ask for constraints before coming up with a logic.

4. Do not lie on the resume or during an interview and be confident in what you know. Make sure you

have an in-depth knowledge of everything you have put on your resume.

5. Practice by giving mock technical and hr interviews.

6. Study the important concepts of OS, CCN, DBMS, OOPS along with a knowledge of system design

concepts.
All the Best!!

Day 1:

• Coding Test

Day 2:

• Technical Round 1

• Technical Round 2

• HR Round

1.
Coding Test [182 Candidates appeared]
Firstly there was a pre-placement talk conducted by PhonePe discussing the various aspects of the company
which was then followed by a coding test.
It was a 90 minute pure coding test consisting of 4 questions.

1. This was a medium/hard string question. We were given a main string (say, m) and two other strings

(say, s1 and s2). Now, we had to create a resulting string such that it is a concatenation of any
number of s1 and any number of s2 (in any order) as long as a character in the resulting string
appears at most as many times as it appears in m. Initially I thought this was a greedy approach using
word frequencies but it seemed more difficult than that so I moved on to the next question. Later I
came back to the question and applied a recursive approach to consider all permutations. As a result I
was able to pass most of the test cases. I wanted to apply the DP approach but I had run out of time
so I was only able to do it partially.

2. This was a hard graph question. The question was also really long so I can't recall it. Eventually I

understood what the question was asking but it would've taken a long time and still I wasn't sure so I
skipped it completely and moved to the questions which I at least had some idea about.

3. This was also a hard tree question. It looked like a greedy question. I thought about an approach but

to me it seemed risky given the time constraints so I moved onto the next question.
--- PAGE 2 ---

4. This was a medium level tree question. You were given a tree, there is a robber at the root node and

each leaf node of the tree consists of a bank. The goal is for the robber to be able to rob as many
banks as possible. However there are also police stations which can appear at any node. Now, we are
given a parameter (say, m) such that the robber can rob any bank as long as the path from the root
node to that bank does not consist of m consecutive police stations. We had to find the maximum
number of banks that could be robbed. This question was easier than the others. I applied a direct
DFS approach along with the necessary conditions. I was able to solve this one.
Finally, 14 candidates were selected for the next round. It looks like the cut off was at least 1 question fully
solved and maybe one partially solved.
Tip: During the test, read each question first and start with those questions which you have an intuition
about.

2. Technical Round 1 [ 14 Candidates appeared]

The round started with the interviewer asking for my introduction and then gave his own introduction. He
also asked me to briefly explain the recent projects I worked on. After explaining, he asked some basic
questions about it, nothing too serious. Next he started with the dsa questions.

1. You are given an array of Characters(only B and F) and a frog positioned at the starting index. The

frog has to reach the ending position. B indicates a backward jump and F indicates a forward jump.
Sample input: FROG | FBBBBFFBBFFB | END
You have to find a minimum threshold jump distance (say, d) such that if the frog lands on an F tile
then it can make a forward jump of at most d (i.e jump length can be between 1 and d, inclusive)
tiles and if it lands on a B tile, it can make a backward jump of at most d tiles. The goal is to find a
minimum threshold jump distance d such that the frog can reach the end.
Firstly, the interviewer made sure that I understood the question. So, after he was finished
explaining, I gave him my understanding of the PS.
I started with the logic, about how the frog can reach the end position. He also gave me a sample test
case to test my approach. Eventually, I told him that since forward jumps are only helpful in this
question, we have to find the distances between consecutive forward jumps. And the maximum
distance between any two consecutives F's is the distance which we will have to cover using a jump
so that would be the answer. After giving this logic, I still thought about the edge cases to see if it
fails. I explained my logic as to why it is necessary to take the maximum. After this he asked me to
write a pseudo code for my approach and then using a sample test case we checked if it works.
Finally he agreed on the approach and moved to the next question.

2. Next was a leetcode question: https://leetcode.com/problems/uncrossed-lines/. This is similar to the

longest common subsequence question.
--- PAGE 3 ---
I started with the brute recursive approach. However, he said that it has exponential complexity so I
added the DP approach to remove redundant computations. However, he wanted the On 2)
approach so I gave him the bottom-up iterative approach. He asked me to give the pseudo code and
told me to first write the DP equations. Since it was a 2D DP problem, he told me to draw the DP
matrix and gave me a sample test case to do a complete dry run. Then he asked me that if we want to
print the matching string then how can we add code for that. I told him we can perform a second pass
doing a backtracking from the bottom right cell in the matrix and reaching the top-left left using the
DP relation. However, he was looking for a solution in a single pass and asked me if that was
possible. I told him that it would not be possible in a single pass. He then asked me about the worst
case time complexity of printing the matched string. I told him it would be O(s1.length + s2.length)
in case there are no matching characters.
I asked him a few questions about his position and work at PhonePe. He then also gave me a scenario about
how one would go about testing and reviewing code they have written. The round ended with a couple more
questions.

3. Technical Round 2[9 Candidates appeared]

The round directly started with a dsa question.
You are given a 2D matrix containing positive and negative integers. You have to find a strictly increasing
sequence of cells such that from the current cell you can move to any cell in the same row or any cell in
the same column. This looked like a DFS + DP problem, so firstly I explained my approach and they
also told me to write the c++ code as well. They also gave me sample cases to test my approach. The
complexity of the solution was O(n) so they told me to improve it. I gave a few other approaches but
they said it was not a significant improvement. They were looking for something with an On') or
O(n'logn) complexity.
This problem took some time but I kept explaining my approaches. They also gave me some hints on how
to proceed. Finally, I was able to optimize it further and come up with an O(n'logn) solution using binary
search and sorting. They told me to write production level cpp code after which the interview ended.

3. HR Round [6 Candidates appeared ]

The round was comparatively pretty chill. He firstly asked me what was my experience with the coding test.
What was the difficulty level and so on. Then he asked for my introduction and then moved onto my
resume. He first asked me about my projects. What was the motivation for the project, what were the
problems we faced, how did we solve them, how much were we able to complete, tech stack used, etc. He
also gave me a few scenarios like how I would distribute work in a team and also asked about any
experience I had where I did not like working on a project because of some problems with a colleague or a
teacher, etc.
After this he went on to my internship. He asked about what product we were building, what was my team
like, what was my contribution as a backend dev, how did we do code reviews, etc. I thoroughly explained
the whole process we followed and also the product I had worked on. He asked whether we used a sql/nosql
DB and why. He asked for my opinion as to why we chose a Nosql DB, and what problems did it solve.
--- PAGE 4 ---
Then he asked what according to me are my 5 strengths/weaknesses and also what are the 5 things I would
improve about myself.
After this he asked me what is the app I frequently use, I said reddit. He then asked questions about how,
according to me, does reddit deal with latency issues and how does it make sure that updates are done in real
time. Since, I did not exactly know how reddit handles all this, I gave him a rough idea of what I think it
might be using. I told him about distributed computing and databases which could be used to deal with
latency and also using cache queues for real time updates. I also explained strong and eventual consistency
and their application in different systems in order to maintain consistent data. He then asked whether I know
about CDNs. I said yes and then explained in brief what they are and their applications. He then gave his
views and experience on the topic.
After that he asked if I had any questions for him. I asked him questions about how phonepe executes an
idea from start to final deployment. I asked about his experience as a former cpp developer. The interview
ended after a couple more questions.
Overall, the HR round was kind of like a discussion about my resume and technology in general along with
a few behavioral questions. The interviewer was also quite friendly.
Finally, 4 candidates received an offer.

Tips:

1. PhonePe interviews are mostly DSA based so make sure to focus more on that. Study the working

and time complexities of all important data structures and algorithms.

2. During the technical interview, make sure to think out loud. It is important that you communicate

your ideas and approaches to the interviewer, since they are interested in your thought process and
logic building. If they know what direction you are thinking in, they can also provide appropriate
hints.

3. When given a dsa question, firstly explain your own understanding of the problem so the interviewer

can make sure you have got it right and also ask for constraints before coming up with a logic.

4. Do not lie on the resume or during an interview and be confident in what you know. Make sure you

have an in-depth knowledge of everything you have put on your resume.

5. Practice by giving mock technical and hr interviews.

6. Study the important concepts of OS, CCN, DBMS, OOPS along with a knowledge of system design

concepts.
All the Best!!

journey.prep:
You don't need to solve all questions to get shortlisted. So, read all questions properly and

then focus on the ones which you are sure you can do.

Technical Interview - Round 1 (15 Shortlisted):

Introduce yourself.
Question 1: Initial capital, max number of projects which can be done, arrays of capital required
by each project and profit generated by each project. Find maximum money possible.
Approach:

• Sort all projects according to capital required (Store capital[index] and index for every

project)

• Declare a Priority Queue -> Comparator : profit[i] - capital[i] -> (Descending order)

• Run a for loop: 0 to k-1

• Add all feasible projects (capital required < current capital) to a Priority Queue

only if profit [1] > capital[1]

• Pop the top and add it to answer.

• Time Complexity: O(nlogn + k)

• Space Complexity: O(n)

Question 2: https://leetcode.com/problems/uncrossed-lines/
I gave a DP solution after a Recursive solution. Then, I wrote the whole code on paper.
I could easily solve both questions. Initially, I was not sure whether I had to maximize the net
capital or the obtained profit so, I clarified it before approaching the solution. Almost everyone
who could solve all questions (2 or 3) asked to them were shortlisted for the next round. This
round lasted for 30-45 minutes.

Tips: Understand the question properly, clarify the constraints, discuss approach (My interviewer

expected me to speak out what I was thinking and how I was approaching the problem), dry run,
write code.
--- PAGE 3 ---

Technical Interview - Round 2 (9 Shortlisted):

General Questions like hobbies, goals, aspirations to start the conversation.
Question 1: A matrix of numbers is given. From each cell, you can jump to any cell in the same
row or in the same column which is strictly greater than the current number. Find the longest
possible path.
Approach:

• Sort all cell values in descending order (Store x and y coordinates for each cell)

• Initialize a rows[r] and cols[c] array to store the max path in each row and column

respectively

• Traverse through the sorted list

• For each element, check max path available, add 1 to it and update the same in

rows and cols arrays

• Time Complexity: O(n*m*log(n*m))

• Space Complexity: O(n*m)

I gave a On*m*(ntm)) solution and then came up with the optimal solution after a hint. I wrote
the whole code after explaining the approach.
Question 2: Solve a Sudoku
An obvious solution would be Backtracking. However, the interviewer asked for a better
solution. He insisted on thinking about maybe a new data structure.
He was simply looking for how you approach such problems. No code was expected, it was only
a discussion. This round lasted for 30-45 minutes.

Tips: Explain what you are thinking. Sometimes, they are just looking for how you approach a

problem. Be very patient while explaining your approach. They might try to confuse you to
check how confident you are about your approach. The best thing to do is to take a test case and
dry run.
Hiring Manager - Round 3(6 Shortlisted):
(No DSA, purely Resume-based, behavioral, and abstract problem solving round)
Started with how the test was and the previous interviews. Then he started asking questions on
my projects.

1. What, Why and How was the project built? Your contribution (for group projects), Did

the project serve the purpose? What more could have been done?

2. Why this field / role ?

--- PAGE 4 ---

3. Frontend or Backend? Why is that? > Backend -> He had mentioned about the difficulty

of handling multiple services at the backend in the PPT. So what do you think is difficult
in the backend?

4. App used frequently - Instagram - Explain how only the stories of the people you follow

are shown to you from millions of stories. Explain how the story bar is designed. How are
advertisements added to it?

5. On basis of my previous answers, I was asked whether I would build a startup in Finance

or Tech if was provided with the required money
This round started with explaining each and every detail written on the Resume. The interviewer
will ask follow up questions based on your answers. Your overall understanding of your projects,
passion for technology, future goals, how you approach unseen problems, how you deal with
counter opinions is tested throughout the interview. This round lasted for more than an hour.

Tips: Structure your answer and then speak, prepare technical as well as business aspects of your

projects. Be Very Honest during the interview. Do NOT lie on your resume.
> 4 candidates received offers (3 - I+FTE and 1 - I)
Be ready with good questions for the interviewers. They spend a considerable time answering
them. I do believe they value the intent and interest shown through the questions.
Stay Calm, Give your best and Enjoy the Process. Best Of Luck!
(Feel free to contact me in case of any queries)
