customSections.content:
You don't need to solve all questions to get shortlisted. So, read all questions properly and

then focus on the ones which you are sure you can do.

Technical Interview - Round 1 (15 Shortlisted):

Introduce yourself.
Question 1: Initial capital, max number of projects which can be done, arrays of capital required
by each project and profit generated by each project. Find maximum money possible.
Approach:

• Sort all projects according to capital required (Store capital[index] and index for every

project)

• Declare a Priority Queue -> Comparator : profit[i] - capital[i] -> (Descending order)

• Run a for loop: 0 to k-1

• Add all feasible projects (capital required < current capital) to a Priority Queue

only if profit [1] > capital[1]

• Pop the top and add it to answer.

• Time Complexity: O(nlogn + k)

• Space Complexity: O(n)

Question 2: https://leetcode.com/problems/uncrossed-lines/
I gave a DP solution after a Recursive solution. Then, I wrote the whole code on paper.
I could easily solve both questions. Initially, I was not sure whether I had to maximize the net
capital or the obtained profit so, I clarified it before approaching the solution. Almost everyone
who could solve all questions (2 or 3) asked to them were shortlisted for the next round. This
round lasted for 30-45 minutes.

Tips: Understand the question properly, clarify the constraints, discuss approach (My interviewer

expected me to speak out what I was thinking and how I was approaching the problem), dry run,
write code.
--- PAGE 3 ---

Technical Interview - Round 2 (9 Shortlisted):

General Questions like hobbies, goals, aspirations to start the conversation.
Question 1: A matrix of numbers is given. From each cell, you can jump to any cell in the same
row or in the same column which is strictly greater than the current number. Find the longest
possible path.
Approach:

• Sort all cell values in descending order (Store x and y coordinates for each cell)

• Initialize a rows[r] and cols[c] array to store the max path in each row and column

respectively

• Traverse through the sorted list

• For each element, check max path available, add 1 to it and update the same in

rows and cols arrays

• Time Complexity: O(n*m*log(n*m))

• Space Complexity: O(n*m)

I gave a On*m*(ntm)) solution and then came up with the optimal solution after a hint. I wrote
the whole code after explaining the approach.
Question 2: Solve a Sudoku
An obvious solution would be Backtracking. However, the interviewer asked for a better
solution. He insisted on thinking about maybe a new data structure.
He was simply looking for how you approach such problems. No code was expected, it was only
a discussion. This round lasted for 30-45 minutes.

Tips: Explain what you are thinking. Sometimes, they are just looking for how you approach a

problem. Be very patient while explaining your approach. They might try to confuse you to
check how confident you are about your approach. The best thing to do is to take a test case and
dry run.

1. First Round [82 students appeared for the test]

The test was conducted on Google Forms in the form of MCQs in the college. There were 70 questions which
had to be solved in 90 minutes. And please note that there was negative marking of 0.25 as well.
Questions: 40 technical and 30 aptitude based.
Technical: 18 Java, 17 Python and 5 MySQL (The questions for Java and python included output -based
questions and abit of theory as well and for MySQL, queries were given as option)
Aptitude: It included bar-graph, pi-chart, age problem, distance problems and the basic aptitude problems.

In the technical part, concepts related to enum and singleton , collections, oops were also asked for Java and
for python questions related to tuple, lists, dictionary were asked . So, try learning the basic concepts of both
the languages as sometimes it will help in solving the easy and straightforward questions of both the languages
as well. For practice, GFG, interviewbit and other websites would be useful.
For MySQL, knowing about joins, group by having clause and subqueries would be useful. Now, for the
technical part, most of the questions were output based questions where the code's picture was giv en and
output was asked.
For the aptitude part, indiabix is one of the useful resources. Practice aptitude questions as it will help you in
solving them quickly during the main test.
If possible, rather than guessing right from start, try solving questions  whose answer you are sure about as
there is negative marking.
The questions in the test were of mixed difficulty and required solving as well. So, it is better to have a practice
in advance.
Also, one approach that I used was to allot time for each section so I could give maximum time to the section
in which I was most confident.

2. Technical Round [23 students were selected for this round]

The interviews were conducted the same day as the test. There were two rounds of interviews: Technical and
HR round. The interview was conducted by two people. Also, this interview mainly dependent on the first
preference you filled while the form for this  company was floated. Like mine was software engineer as the
first preference. And for me, this round lasted for about 45 min to 50 mins.
The interview started with my introduction where I had mentioned my projects so I explained about it in short
as well. Then, they started straightaway with the interview. One thing which I felt was that the interviews
easily understood how much confident we were in any concept. So, they would ask in depth for the ones which
we knew but not in depth as well.
They started by asking my major programming language which was Java and they asked about the 4 pillars
of OOPS and with the words they were satisfied and they moved on to upcasting and downcasting in Java.
And this is the question which I was asked in every interview which I appeared so ensure you know that. The
basic concept is which methods and variables are acces sible if we make object of parent class and use child
class constructor and vice versa.
Then a basic java program was asked to me which was to count distinc t words in a string which can be done
using HashMap. This led to a follow-up question of if I want to insert elements in insertion order which would
be used and it would be linkedHashMap and why not TreeMap So, a good knowledge of Collections is a must
if your major programming language is Java. Then a common question to me and candidate before me was
asked which was if you have a list of objects of employees which has the department and salary stored in it,
how will you calculate average salary per department. So, one of the approaches was that using two hashmaps,
it can be done where one would store the number of employees per department and another would store the
total salary of the employees of that department. And then basic questions related to Java were asked so have
solid points to answer when asked any questions.
This was then followed by MySQL and MongDB related questions as I had mentioned both in resume. The
difference between NoSQL and RDBMS. The generation of unique ID in MongoDB document and w hether
it can be updated, type of nosql database mongodb is, difference between collection and document. Basic
queries of how MongoDB works like and how connection is done. For MySQL, they were interested in how
to connect mysql with Java which can be done by downloading JDBC driver and also know how whole process
takes place like for connection like the components in connection query which contains the username,
password and all. For query, a simple group by having clause query was asked and the order of e xecution of
select, group by, having, where was asked. Also, a major discussion went on the topic of difference between
unique not null key and primary key and whether null can be used multiple times in unique key or it cannot
be considered even once. So, regarding these questions, make a note in your book as due to the interview
pressure, one might get them wrong. Also, if they feel that we know the answer but are confused regarding
the same, they would give small hints.
And then they asked whether about REST API and the methods of rest and how is the request of get and put
works.
The interview ended with they asking whether I had any questions so I asked them regarding the tech stacks
and the latest projects they were working on. It was altogether a very  good interactive interview which felt
more like a discussion. And incase if you don't know any concept or answer, tell them honestly so they can
move on with next question.

3. HR Round [7 students were selected for this round]

In this round basic HR quest ions were asked after I gave my introduction which was less technical and I
mentioned about my education as they had told me what all they want to know about me in my
introduction. Apart from that, they asked whether I would like to pursue higher studies and why not. They
asked me about my preference between working full stack and only backend. It was then followed by what
would I choose between working on different programming languages or different databases irrespective
of the language. In my resume, I had mentioned about my minor course of management from SPJIMR, so
they were interested to know about that. And the basic question of why ISS was asked. It ended with me
asking few questions about the company.
It was comparatively a short interview but a goo d experience. General piece of advice would be that for
this round, don't mug up any answer but keep in mind what all points you would say if any kind of
questions are asked.

At the end, all 7 students were selected.

Section A:

Condition :- a) if the length of numbers are <=3 then find average and print
b) if length >3 then find average of latest 3 elements
Eg. :-
Input -
5 //output 5
15 //output 10 (avg(5,10))
10 // output 10 (avg(5,15,10))
5 // output 10 (avg(15,10,5))
9 // output 8 (avg(10,5,9))
So on… (size is not defined)

3. Given n. print the union of prime numbers less than n and Fibonacci numbers less than n.

Eg - n=10
Prime numbers :- 2 3 5 7
Fibonacci :- 0 1 1 2 3 5 8
Output :- 0 1 2 3 5 7 8

4. Question was on DP. Given an array of position of houses and you have to arrange 4 people in

such a way that at most distance between adjacent people should not be more than m. find the no.
of ways for such arrangement.

I did both questions in section 1 and one question in section 2. A total of 15 students qualified for the
next round.

2. Technical Interview (Offline) (about 1hr 15 min) (25th July)

This round was conducted in their andheri office.  There were two interviewers. The interview was
mainly focused on basics of C++. And some DSA questions. Make sure to clear each concept in c++
right from clas ses to STL. They asked about o ops and then polymorphism . They asked me to write
down code for every example. Then they asked me about inherit ance and its types. What will be the
size of an empty class, which functions are present in class by default, virtual class, etc.

Then they came towards data structures and asked me to write code to implement stack using queue. I
firstly got confused and told that I will use array t o implement stack but they want implementation
using queue only. I thought for a while and gave one approach using queue. They seemed to be satisfied
by that approach.

Then they grilled me on pointers.  Asked me many tricky questions on pointers. Use of malloc, calloc,

function for that approach and asked me time complexity for that function. I wrote basic definition of
recursive function in merge sort and luckily, he seemed quite happy with that and told me if I had any
questions for them.

To tackle this round you must have a good practice of dsa problem. Practicing dsa questions in leetcode will

2. Technical round ( more than 1 hour )

This round happened at their Andheri office, and there were two interviewers present. The interview
started with the classic "Tell me about yourself." After my introduction, the interviewers asked about
memory management in C and C++. They wanted to know about calloc and malloc, what they return,
how many things they take as input, and the differences between them. They also asked about the
distinctions between free in C and delete in C++.
Moving on to object-oriented programming (OOP), they asked how to access private members of a class.
While I mentioned getter and setter methods and friend functions, they hinted at another way using
pointers, but I didn't fully understand it at the time. They then discussed compile-time polymorphism and
runtime polymorphism, specifically talking about virtual functions. They wanted an explanation of
function overriding and how the program decides which function (from the base class or child class) to
--- PAGE 2 ---
call. I had some idea about a virtual pointer (vptr) and virtual table, so I explained them as best as I
could.
They emphasized that a solid understanding of OOP is crucial since they asked detailed questions on each
topic. After the OOP part, they talked about pointers. They asked me to explain the difference between
references and pointers, create pointers to structures and classes, and explain how much memory a
pointer variable uses. They also asked why it's important to mention the data type when declaring a
pointer-this is essential for something called pointer arithmetic.
Then they asked about accessing data using pointers, which means dereferencing. Moving on to template
classes and the Standard Template Library (STL), they wanted me to explain what templates are in C++,
how vector and map work, the idea behind hashing, and how to deal with collisions in hash-based data
structures.

my preferred programming language and the reasons behind my choice. Towards the end of the
interview, she asked if I had any questions for her, and I inquired about the training process for new
joiners at the company.

5. Start your placement preparation in advance, do not wait for the last months as you will not have

time to cover up so many concepts once the companies start coming. Practice DSA daily on
whichever platform you prefer like Leetcode, CodeChef, etc. You should be aware of all the data
structures. Also have in depth knowledge of your primary language.

6. Refer GFG, Brainstellar for puzzles, InterviewBit, javatpoint, GFG for revising your OOPS, OS,

DBMS concepts, IndiaBix for aptitude. Prepare for aptitude really well, do not take it lightly as most
of the companies have aptitude, verbal reasoning as a part of their assessment.

7. Coming to the HR questions, just google HR interview questions and you will get a list. Prepare

sample answers for these questions in advance. These are more like the personal response questions,
just remember not to brag about yourself, be humble and answer these questions. Do not tell them
about your higher education plans even if you have one :)

knowledge of the company, what it does, recent news about the company, values of the company, etc.

know your approach and how you go about solving the problem, they analyze you on your problem
solving skills. If you do not recall the answer, tell them politely, sometimes they might give you
some hints. Do not be in a hurry to answer the questions, take a pause, think about the answer
properly and then answer.

in turn affect your preparation. Instead of burdening yourself with the rejection you faced in one
company, think where you can improve and start preparing yourself for the next company that visits.

Durvesh Chaudhari
ETRX

Company - Oracle

Job Profile - Associate Application Developer

Offer Type - Placement Only

CTC - 19.18 LPA (14.5 Base + ESOP + PF/PPF + Gratuity)

Location - Mumbai / Pune / Bangalore / Chennai

❖ Placement Process -

1. Online Assessment Round (Coding and Aptitude) -

In total, there were 22 questions during the round, comprising 10 quantitative, 10 verbal, 1 medium
difficulty coding, and 1 easy API question. The quantitative and verbal questions were straightforward,
and the round lasted for 100 minutes.

Coding Question - Lexicographically Largest Subsequence
API Question - REST API: Asteroid Orbit

2. Interviews -

• Technical Round - 1

In this round, I was among the 49 students selected, and the interview focused solely on evaluating
our resumes. The session lasted for about 40 minutes, and it kicked off with the classic "Tell me
about Yourself" question. I had prepared extensively for this question to steer the interview in the
direction I wanted. The interviewer then proceeded to read my resume and asked specific questions
about all the projects I had listed.

As Python was my primary language, the interviewer inquired about the differences between tuples
and lists, and also asked me about Python's dynamically typed nature. I confidently answered these
questions, which seemed to satisfy the interviewer.

Next, the interviewer delved into Database Management Systems (DBMS) topics and asked about
indexing and ACID properties. I provided satisfactory responses to these queries.

Following that, the interviewer presented a coding question, asking me to swap two variables
without using a third variable. I quickly came up with a solution using the addition and subtraction
method, and the interviewer seemed pleased with my answer. However, the interviewer then
proposed an alternative approach involving multiplication and division, and asked me to analyse
which one was better. I pointed out the potential error risks in the division-based approach,
reaffirming the superiority of my initial solution.

Afterwards, the interviewer challenged me with a medium difficulty question Rotate Array. He also
asked me different types of Tree Traversal techniques.

Given my background in Computer Networks, the interviewer asked me to state the different layers
in the TCP/IP protocol, which I answered accurately. Additionally, because of my Electronics
background, the interviewer inquired about the difference between a Microprocessor and a
Microcontroller. Although I must admit I wasn't fully prepared for this question, I provided a
partially correct answer. However, the interviewer corrected me, and we engaged in a constructive
discussion about the topic. Later he asked me a puzzle - 9 balls.

At the end of the round, 28 students, including myself, were shortlisted for the next stage of the
selection process.

• Technical Round 2 -

During this round, which lasted for approximately 30 to 35 minutes, the interviewer started by
asking me to introduce myself. Since I had mentioned that I took a Foundational course in
Programming and Data Science from IITM, the interviewer inquired whether I was still continuing
the course and what I had learned from it. They then asked me to explain Normal Distribution
without using any technical terms and with a simple example, as if I were explaining it to a ten-
year-old. Similarly, I was asked to explain Queue and Priority Queue using non-technical language
and examples.
After that, the interviewer asked about the time complexity of inserting, popping, and accessing an
element in both the Queue and Priority Queue data structures. Following this, they asked me with a
medium difficulty DSA question: finding the Kth largest number in an unsorted array. Initially, I
provided a brute force approach by suggesting to sort the array. The interviewer acknowledged that
it was correct but encouraged me to optimize the solution. I then proceeded to solve the question
using a Priority Queue and even wrote the code for it on paper.
Finally, the interviewer asked me if I have any question for them and ended the interviewer.

• HR Interview Round -

This interview lasted for around 20 minutes. During the interview process, we were split into two
groups and conducted interviews on different floors. As the day was coming to an end, some
students, did not have the HR round scheduled. On my floor 6-7 students were selected for this
round.
In this round, there were two interviewers, and although it was supposed to be an HR interview, one
of the interviewers surprised me by asking about procedures in Database Management Systems
(DBMS). I wasn't familiar with this concept, I admitted that and I tried turning it into a constructive
discussion. The interviewer was kind enough to explain the concept to me.
The same interviewer then asked me to explain Doubly Linked List with an example. I provided an
explanation to the best of my knowledge, and the interview proceeded smoothly. The other
interviewer focused on HR-related questions, inquiring about my family background and my future
plans for the next 5 or 10 years. Additionally, they questioned why I didn't use Java as my primary
programming language, even though I had studied it in my 5th semester. I confidently explained
that due to the IITM course, Python became my first programming language, and I became
comfortable with it. However, I reassured them that I was proficient in Java as well and could easily
switch between languages based on the requirements. I made sure to convince them that language
was not a barrier for me, and I was adaptable and competent in both Python and Java.
Then he asked me if I have any questions for him.
Finally, 17 students were selected.

❖ Tips -

1. Interviews will always start by asking to introduce yourself. So, prepare well for this question.

2. Know your resume well and do not add anything that you don't know about.

3. Be clear and confident while answering to the questions.

4. Communication is the key. Don't just answer. Try to build a conversation with interviewer.

5. Knowing Java is not necessity. But make sure to convince them that you are flexible to change the

language if needed.

6. When asked a dsa question, start by giving them a brute force. While solving keep communicating

what you are thinking and your approach to solve the question. Then after brute force, give them an
optimised approach. Give them a dry run of your code by running few test cases.

7. If you don't know the answer, admit it and try to get into a discussion and show them that you are

interested in learning.

8. Practice few easy for building base, and majorly medium questions on leetcode.

Feel free to connect on LinkedIn.
All the Best!!

code to fetch data of countries from the given API. This question was easy to solve. Most of the people
who got selected had solved both of these questions, so aim to complete both of them.

2. Technical Round 1(35-40 minutes)

This round consisted of 49 students who were selected from the test. We were first given a pre placement
talk after which the interviews started. The interviewing panel consisted of 2 individuals. They started by
asking me to introduce myself. They made sure that the environment was very friendly and made sure
that I was not nervous. They asked me questions purely based on my resume. They started with my
projects and how I had contributed to them. Simple questions like what is redux, which version of node
did I use were asked. They also asked me about Git commands and if I knew what SVN is (Version
Control). After that they moved onto RDBMS, asked me which I would prefer while making a project.
Then they asked me which type of DB would be best suited for Instagram. I also had mentioned a
hackathon on my resume so they asked me about my contribution to it. Then they moved to DSA. I was
asked the missing number problem. After this I was asked which is the best sorting algorithm for a
partially sorted array, to which I replied Insertion sort and I was asked to code the same. The last
question was about tree traversals. I was asked to write the pseudo code for Level Order Traversal which
I did and the interview ended there.
After Round 1, I was the first to be called for Round 2 and it happened immediately after the previous
round.
--- PAGE 2 ---

3. Technical Round 2(30 minutes)

This round was shorter than the previous round. Again, this round started with the interviewer asking me
to introduce myself. I had mentioned that I play chess so we had a short conversation about that. All the
interviewers were very friendly and made sure that I was comfortable. There was only 1 person in the
panel this time. He asked me about the CNN algorithm, since I had used it in one of my projects. Then
he moved on to DSA. Again, I was asked Tree traversals, BFS/DFS and how all of them work. The next
question was Dutch National Flag. I had previously solved this question on leetcode. He had framed a
story: There is a school annual day and students, teachers and parents are all invited. There is a line of
chairs arranged and everyone randomly sits in any of the chairs. I have to sort them in such a way that all
students sit together, all teachers sit together and so do the parents. He gave me 5 minutes to think about
this question. He made me realize that I can do better than merge sort. First I gave him the counting
approach which was correct but he wasn't satisfied with it. So I used a 2 pointer approach by swapping,
which was what he wanted. He asked me if I knew the name of the problem since it is very famous, but I
was unaware about it. The interview ended here.
HR round was not conducted for me and many other students, but this does not eliminate you from the
process. A total of 17 people were selected after the whole process was completed.

A total of 47 students were shortlisted for the interviews. The shortlist was released the evening

Pre-Placement Talk (28th July) 9:30 AM (Offline)
The Oracle team introduced us to Oracle and explained to us about OFSS. They then opened the

Round 2: Technical Interview (28th July) (47 Candidates)

My interview was a pretty chill one and there were 3 interviewers. It started around 11 am. It
took around 35-40 minutes to complete my interview. I was introduced with a warm smile and
they seemed friendly. They made me comfortable and asked me to introduce myself. After that
they asked me a bit about why I chose EXTC engineering, and why Oracle. Please answer this
question in the most diplomatic manner possible, so that you don't leave any negative
impressions. Also they asked me about my prior work experience, which I didn't have.
Then they asked me to solve a DSA related question. They asked me to implement Stack using
Linked List. They asked me to write the code (or pseudocode works too) on a paper. I solved the
question. There were a few places where I got stuck, or they purposely put me in a state of
confusion, but I was confident about my piece of code so they didn't grind me on that. They were
helpful and I got through that question and they were pretty satisfied, telling me that I was 90%
accurate.
They then asked me to draw the wireframe or UI of one of my projects which was a simple
front-end website, and then asked me about what Bootstrap is, which I used in that project.
Then they asked me about the programming languages I've learnt in my engineering and also
about my most favorite subject and why. This round was pretty good for me. It was like a group
discussion with the interviewers.

This round was totally technical. It started around 2 pm. There was only 1 interviewer and he
seemed quite experienced. He first asked me about the difference between Graphs and Trees.
Then he asked some more questions on graphs. He asked me about topological sort, but I didn't

find the pairs of anagrams in the array. I explained to him my approach of sorting every string

My 3rd round took place immediately after my 2nd round ended, just having a gap of a few
minutes. It was taken by the Vice President of OFSS. He was very friendly and encouraging. He
initially made me comfortable and then asked me about which language is more Object oriented-
C++ or Java. Then he asked me some basic concepts of OOPS. After that he asked me about
pointers.
After that the technical aspect was done and he asked me basic HR questions like "Where do you
see yourself in the next 2-4-8-10 years? " I answered it and then he asked me about my
willingness to relocate to Bangalore. Finally he asked me about my plans for higher studies.

• Even though the position is for App Developer, they do not expect you to know any App

Development beforehand.

• The interviewers want to know you more, so try to open up as much as possible and have

a discussion, rather than an anxious interview.

• Doesn't matter if you have prior work experience or not, they just want to check your

problem solving skills, your hunger to keep learning and your attitude towards solving a
given problem.

• Especially for EXTC folks, it doesn't matter if you have hardware projects in your

resume, you just have to know each and everything about those projects.

• If you get stuck on a given question, just tell them your approach, and they'll give you

hints. If you totally don't know an algorithm that they asked, just be honest and tell them.
Do not panic.

• Your Luck matters a lot, so don't be dejected if you do not get selected even if you gave

your best, there's a bigger opportunity waiting for you!
All the best!!

journey.prep:
● Practice, practice and practice. Begin your placement preparation early, as waitinguntil the last few months won't leave you enough time to cover all the necessaryconcepts. Dedicate time daily to practice Data Structures and Algorithms (DSA) onplatforms like LeetCode or GFG, give contests and have a strong grasp of your

primary programming language. Alongside, compare these algorithms you've usedin your projects.

● To be honest, I started seriously concentrating on DSA only around 2-3 monthsbefore my placements(which I still regret). However, if you're in a similar situation,don't panic. Put in dedicated and consistent effort, even if you have limited time forpreparation. Practice like hell and stay committed in the days leading up to yourplacements.

● Devote consistent practice to aptitude for 1-2 months before placements. Takeaptitude and verbal reasoning seriously, as these are commonly included inassessments by many companies.

● Master CCN, OOPS, and your core language (Java, C++, Python) listed on yourresume. Be thoroughly prepared in advance for OS, DBMS, and SQL, as these arefundamental. Utilize resources like GFG, InterviewBit, and Javatpoint to reviewOOPS, OS, and DBMS. Additionally, enhance your aptitude skills through platformslike IndiaBix. regularly

● Be completely familiar with your resume content. Understand every aspect,including projects and tools. Honesty is crucial; don't claim knowledge you lack. When discussing a group project, outline the project first, then clarify yourindividual contribution. Avoid mentioning topics you're not confident about, asinterviewers may probe further.

● Prepare your response to the "Introduce yourself" question in advance, as it shapesthe direction of the interview conversation.. Note down the questions to ask theinterviewer during the interview in PPT. Familiarize yourself with the company'sbackground, its activities, recent updates, and its principles. This will help youengage in meaningful discussions and show your interest in the company.

● For the HR questions, create a list of possible HR questions and answers and keep ithandy. Review these questions as you get closer to your placement interviews.

● During interviews, it's not necessary to have all the right answers. Interviewers aremore interested in how you approach problems and solve them. They're assessingyour problem-solving skills. If you don't remember an answer, it's okay to admit itpolitely. Sometimes, interviewers might offer hints. Remember, there's no rush toanswer quickly. Take a moment, think through your response, and then reply. Theinterviewers might try to confuse you so at that time be calm and answer carefully.

● Don't let stress overwhelm you during placement season, as it can make you feeldrained and impact your preparation. Instead of dwelling on rejections from onecompany, focus on where you can improve and get ready for the next opportunity. Remember, luck plays a role too, so if you're not selected, it doesn't mean you're notgood enough - the company might be missing out on a fantastic employee.

● Maintain a positive demeanor and always wear a smile. Project confidence in yourresponses, even when addressing incorrect answers.

References:

journey.howSecured:
1. Digital Interview (26 - 31 July)

2. Technical Test (5 August)

3. Group Discussion (7 August, 8:30 - 9:30 AM)

4. Personal Interview (7 August, 10:30 AM onwards)

5. Leadership Interview (7 August)

1.
DI - Digital Interview (Online) - All the applied students appeared for this round
This round was conducted using the Hire Vue Digital Interview platform. You will be given a set number of
questions to answer within a time limit. You will be given a limited amount of time (in out case 30s-1min) to
prepare and formulate your answer and around 3 min to present your answer. It was completely online and
you can give it anytime suitable for you within the deadline mentioned.
A link will be mailed to you with the redirect to the Hire Vue website and further instructions will be provided
accordingly. In our case, the following were the questions:

1. Why did you choose this degree program?

2. What do you aim to gain from this internship?

3. Tell us about a challenging project experience.

4. How did you manage multiple priorities and time?

5. Tell us about a time when you realized you have a weakness and how did you try to overcome that?

6. What'd you like us to know more about you?

--- PAGE 2 ---
This round tested our communication skills, our fluency, and our honesty. Make sure you read a few tips and
research about the interviews given on such platforms before giving your interview. Putting down some of
the resources that I referred to before my Digital Interview.
Pre-Recorded Interview Tips:

1. Dress Professionally

2. Wear headphones and Mic

3. Make sure no background noises or distractions

4. Speak Clearly and Concisely, and Avoid rushing

5. Smile, be positive, look interested, and maintain good body posture

6. Look into the WebCam, not the Screen. You can also blur your video if you are uncomfortable.

7. Prepare answers to the most common questions

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cl9- xVQ800
Note: Do not use ChatGPT, any AI tool, or even read any scripted answers (You can refer some model
answers and use STAR type of methodologies, but make sure it's unique to you and not any generalized
answer). These all recorded interviews are scanned individually and manually by the hiring team. During our
time, such students were immediately rejected and reported to the TPO. So, make sure you BE HONEST,
CONFIDENT, and TRUTHFUL. They volue this the most!

2. Technical Test - Around 100 candidates were shortlisted for this round

The technical exam was conducted using the Microsoft Forms platform. It included 25 MCQs about DSA,
the time complexity of provided code snippets, several aptitude questions (basic), SQL, relational schema,
and a few questions about AI/ML and sorting algorithms. 71 students were chosen for further consideration
after this.
Tips for this round:

1. Practice some basic question types related to Aptitude questions from Indiabix or GFG.

2. Revise all sorting algorithms, their time complexities, and comparisons.

3. Study all data structures and algorithms clearly and try to take some quizzes or practice tests related to

their MCQS.

4. Understand how to calculate the time complexity of a given code snippet and practice it.

--- PAGE 3 ---

3. Group Discussion - 71 students appeared for this round

In this round, all 71 students were divided into groups of 10 each, and a GD panel was assigned. It was
scheduled for early morning 7:30 am. Each group was allotted rooms to sit and proceed with the GD. Our
group was the first panel and it was supposed to start at 8 am. But due to internet connectivity problems and
issues, it began around 8:45 am. Our group topic was - Generative Al: Boon or Bane? We were given 5
minutes for preparation and 10-12 minutes to present the GD.
During the GD, I tried to make a good start but was interrupted, so I gave the other person a chance and
respectfully continued the discussion. I placed one point across in the GD and stressed on the importance of
upskilling and adapting to the AI. Lastly, I made sure that I conclude the GD and gave a brief summary of all
the points that were discussed. I made certain that my delivery was clear and straightforward. My conclusion
was to adequately summarize the important discussion points.
The topics were mostly common ranging from Al, ChatGPT, EV and its evolution and adaptability in India
and its existence, etc. The topics differed somewhat but the central theme was either Al or EV.
After this round, around 4 students from each group were shortlisted.
Tips for GD:

1. Go through the current most hot topics in technology. Refer to the most asked GD questions and

topics through searching. I referred to this link

2. Have a pen and paper ready. As soon as you get the topic, jot down all the points that you can think

about and can talk about in the GD. This will help you focus more on the GD than on collecting your
thoughts during the discussion. Also write the points discussed throughout the GD to make an
impactful, apt, concise, and precise conclusion to the conversation.

3. Be o starter or finisher. Creates an impact on the panel and gives the feeling of a person who takes

the initiative

4. In case, it's not possible, follow up on the conversation and put forward valid points. Make sure the

points that you put are unique and not just paraphrased statements of each other's statements.

5. Try to steer the conversation into a new perspective if you think it's saturating. This will improve the

quality as well as quantity of the conversation and make you stand out from the crowd

6. Don't talk very much or very little. Be apt and clear in your thoughts and speaking.

7. Be confident und be open to understanding other people's perspectives. Make sure you are not

interrupting anyone and giving everybody a chance to speak their minds.

8. If you want to disagree to a point, say politely and put forward an argument.

Remember - This is a GD, not a Debate!

9. If you agree and want to add more to that, do so. That is one of the best ways to insert yourself into

the conversation.

10. Keep smiling and cheerful throughout the conversation and make sure you look fully indulged and

listening to the other people.
Note: If you are not well experienced and have not participated much in GD, go to our IPO or
communication skills professor and ask to conduct Mock GD sessions. This will help you boost your
confidence and give you an idea about your drawbacks. I had got a similar topic in my GD which I had
prepared in a Mock GD. This helped me to confidently put forward my views and ideas without hesitation.
--- PAGE 4 ---

4. Technical Interview - 28 people were interviewed in this round.

There were 3 panels set up, each panel consisting of 2 people. Each panel was equally assigned 7 candidates
which were carefully divided for each panel using their resumes (I suppose). This round began at 10:30 am.
My panel was taking very long interviews. I waited a long time before my interview, at least 5 hours. Some
of the early interviewed people had gone through their next round as well and we were stuck with even the
first round yet to be done. Finally, my interview call came at around 3:30 pm.
My interview started with the constant - Tell me something about yourself/Introduce yourself a question.
While I was answering this question, the interviewers went through my resume and highlighted some of the
points. I supposed that they would stress out on those. One interviewee was on a laptop and the other one had
pen and paper to ask questions. During my introductions, I strongly stressed on my interest and knowledge in
the field of cybersecurity.
So, the first question came through about - Can you explain to me the meaning of inquisitive (Since I had
mentioned it in my intro)? I gave an apt answer about the meaning. Next, the interviewer asked - What is
XSS? I was a bit surprised as I did not expect to get a question on cybersecurity as I did not experience any
such scenario in the earlier interviews. However, I knew all about this and I answered this question
confidently. Next, the interviewers followed with some questions on Linux commands and gave me scenarios
to ask about optimized commands to give the required output. I was able to answer those questions well.
Then the interviewer asked about my internship experience as a Cybersecurity Intern and I elaborated more
on it. Followingly, they asked me how would I proceed to do penetration testing on an E-commerce website
like Amazon (As the interviewer himself was working on an e-commerce website project). I gave all my
process and the vulnerable endpoints that I will scan and he seemed somewhat satisfied with my answer.
Next, the other interviewer read through my profile. He asked me about some of the tools that I had
mentioned related to cybersecurity and hacking.
Next, he asked me whether I wanted some more questions and my interest was more in Networking or Web
App Development. I gave my strong hold of Networking and he asked me further questions related to that.
The questions were about the OSI model, its layers, protocols in each layer, and all the other intricacies. I
stumbled and fumbled a bit on a subnetting question but he guided me through as my approach was clear but
the final answer wasn't accurate. Apart from that, the complete interview was great.
The interviewer also asked about the Minor Degree Management course that I was pursuing at SPJIMR and
how I managed my time throughout the course. What was my daily routine and what recreational activities
do you do and manage my time for that too? Lastly, the interviewer asked me about - Why should we hire
you? In my answer, I focused on my inquisitive nature and elaborated on how I am open to new opportunities
and challenges.
I asked them a question about the work culture and cybersecurity team of Baker Hughes and its details. They
provided me with a very good gist about their team. This concludes the interview. It took place for at least 45
minutes.
I thoroughly enjoyed the interview as it was my first time in on-campus placements where the interview
comprised of what I was interested in and had in-depth knowledge about. It was a really exciting and
insightful experience.
--- PAGE 5 ---

5. Leadership Round - 15 candidates appeared for this round

Immediately after the Technical round, I was asked to present 2 copies of my resume for the next round. I
was instructed to be ready and enter the room to interview after 5 minutes. The panel consisted of 2
interviewers. It was more like a Techno-HR interview.
As soon as I entered the room, I was greeted by the interviewers and I also greeted them. The first question
was - Can you give me a run-through of your resume without glancing at it? I had a complete map of it so I
started off and continued very smoothly. I gave a run through my education, work experience, projects,
achievements, languages, skills, tools, and some leadership role experience. This took at least 15-20 minutes
with all the discussion which followed after each point that I presented.
After this, the interviewer asked me about my hobbies. I told them that I was very much interested in sports
like cricket, volleyball, tennis, table tennis and actively followed F1. I also told about my interest in Music,
singing and that I play the Flute. He asked me - What do you understand by a Hobby? I told them that a
hobby is a task and when I do it, I feel immense pleasure and happiness and satisfaction. He further continued
on asking me questions about F1 as I showed my interest in it. He asked me about which team has done the
fastest pitstop and what was the time. I exactly knew the answer, so I confidently told - Redbull, 1.9secs.
However, the man asked if I was sure and even told me that I am wrong. But I was very sure about my
answer so I told him that I am very confident about it. (PS: Stay on your answer, this shows that you are
confident and will not stumble if counter-questioned). A few more guesstimates type questions on F1
followed namely - What is the weight of an F1 car? How many parts does an F1 car consist of? Here they
check your analytical skills and your approach toward problem-solving.
Next, the interviewer asked questions about some of the terms I had mentioned in my Resume related to IRP,
BCP, and DRP. I explained my understanding and there were some cross questions on it. On answering some
of the questions, the other interviewer, gave a grin and told - "Your answers are not very right, but I like your
confidence!"
. This was a bit weird comment but I liked to take the positive of it :).
They also asked about the Barclays Data Stellar Hackathon, why were you in the Top5, what was your
project and problem statement and about the overall experience. I answered by presenting my part in the
project related to security and told them that it was a main differentiating factor for the qualification in the
Top 5 teams. They seemed very satisfied with the answer. We were slowly going toward the HR questions.
She asked me what was my role as a TPO and what did I do in my position. There was also a question about
why did I leave TPO and do I wish to join it again. I answered that politely with a positive answer and
outlook. Nevertheless, the panel moved on as it became a bit uncomfortable (PS: Be patient if you face
something similar and try to be as honest and positive as possible)
Finally, the panel asked me how would team members look at me if I was a part of the hackathon team. I
answered this by being blatantly honest and completely in full control of my words as it was defining answer
for my personality. Followingly, I was asked about a failure and how did I overcome it. So, I gave an
anecdote about my cricket experience and how I came through this situation and stood strong once again. The
panel then finally asked me to link this answer to any professional or technical aspect of my life where I felt
so. So I compared it to the race of placements where I had prepped my whole year in cybersecurity while the
crowd was focusing on DSA and Web Development.
--- PAGE 6 ---
This was the final question. Then I asked about the growth opportunities that Baker Hughes provides to all its
employees and interns. The lady gave a very insightful answer to this question and I was very convinced that
the company had a great work culture and positive atmosphere with great growth opportunities.
This interview was also around 45 min - 1 hour long.
Finally, & students were selected in Baker Hughes. I was one of them!
This complete day was a very tiring journey that tested everything from initial patience, Technical skills,
knowledge, personality, and even your thinking.

1. Digital Interview (Online)

The digital interviews were conducted on the Hire Vue platform. Following are the questions that
were asked

1. Explain why my background and experience will be a good fit for this job?

2. Why did you decide on your degree program?

3. What do you want to gain from this internship?

4. How did I organize my time if I was given multiple priorities?

5. Tell me about a time when you realized you have a weakness and how did you try to overcome

that?

6. If there's something more we need to know about you?

Each question has 30 sec to prepare and a maximum of 3 mins to answer 1 attempt only per
question.
--- PAGE 2 ---
Be assured in your response, without hesitation or filler words. Maintain fluency while speaking.
Only a limited number of students were not chosen. 107 students were selected for the next
round.

2. Technical Test (20 Questions 30 Minutes) 107 students gave the technical test

The technical test was administered via the Microsoft Forms platform. It comprised 20
multiple-choice questions (MCQs) that focused on topics such as data structures (predominantly
trees/graphs), the time complexity of provided code snippets, several aptitude questions
primarily centered around probability, as well as a few questions related to Al/ML and sorting
algorithms. 71 students were shortlisted for further process.

3. Group Discussion (15 minutes)

A total of 71 students were organized into groups of 10 or 11 each. Each group deliberated on
diverse topics assigned to their respective panels. The topics encompassed discussions like
Electric Vehicles vs. Hybrid Vehicles, The Future of Electric Vehicles, Reasons for the Decline
of Digital Education, and several other subjects related to these themes. Use of the internet was
not allowed, only 2 minutes were given to prepare once the topic of GD was disclosed.
In the group discussion, I managed to contribute once despite facing two interruptions, I
encouraged others to share their views. In the end, when asked to summarize, I ensured a fluent
and concise delivery. The conclusion I provided aimed to encapsulate the key discussion points
effectively.
From every group, 4 students were selected for further rounds.
Tips for Effective Group Discussions:

• Active Listening: Pay attention to others while they speak. This shows respect and

enables you to respond thoughtfully.

• Clear Expression: Speak clearly and confidently. Express your thoughts concisely to

avoid confusion.

• Valuable Contributions: Add value to the discussion by offering unique insights,

examples, or counterarguments that enhance the conversation.
--- PAGE 3 ---

• Respectful Interaction: Treat every participant's viewpoint with respect, even if you

disagree. Avoid interrupting or dominating the conversation.

• Time Management: Keep track of time to ensure everyone gets an opportunity to speak.

Avoid lingering on a single point for too long.

• Balanced Participation: Encourage quieter members to contribute and ensure that the

discussion is inclusive.

• Summarization: Towards the end, provide a brief summary of the key points discussed to

conclude the conversation effectively.
28 students were shortlisted for further process.

4. Technical Interview (Personal Interview : 1 hour)

The session began with a self-introduction. I shared that I had recently begun focusing on
problem-solving, three months prior to the placements. When queried about my choice of timing
for mastering data structures, I clarified that my primary focus lay in development. I highlighted
my accomplishments in various hackathons as well. Subsequently, I was prompted to list and rate
my skills. Questions related to my projects followed, including discussions on algorithm choices,
my preference for React over other frameworks, my contributions, and encountered challenges. I
fielded inquiries about the technical skills I had outlined earlier, involving CSS concepts like the
distinctions between div and span, margin and padding differences, methods for centering a div
tag, and the utility of display flex. JavaScript queries came next, covering topics like the
differences between let, const, and var, as well as the transformation of JSX to JS. Delving
deeper into frontend development, I explained the operational flow of a React application. Later,
leveraging my "problem solver" skill, I was presented with a puzzle involving a man living on
the 7th floor, https://www.puzzlesandriddles.com/LateralThinking13.html which I answered
convincingly. The interviewers were pleased with my response. The technical segment continued
with questions on data structures and algorithms, including linked list operations, stack
functionalities, and binary search tree construction. I confidently addressed each query. I had one
of my projects on encryption algorithms, so I was also asked questions related to end to end
encryption of whatsapp and a few questions related to certain scenarios. Towards the conclusion,
I discussed my strengths and weaknesses. I concluded the interview by inquiring about the
--- PAGE 4 ---
company's resilience during economic downturns, their specific domains within Baker Hughes,
and the organization's commendable achievement in reducing carbon emissions by 31%.
The exchange was thorough and comprehensive, reflecting my adeptness in both
problem-solving and technical domains.
15 students were shortlisted for HR round

5. HR Interview (Leadership Interview: 45 minutes)

The interview followed a Techno-HR format, involving a pair of interviewers. Commencing with
a personal touch, they inquired about my day's experiences. Subsequently, they delved into the
topic of the Group Discussion, probing the points I had raised. Project-related inquiries ensued,
with a focus on their implementation details and the challenges encountered. Of particular
interest were my victorious project from a hackathon and my contribution to the official
undergraduate college website. They keenly explored the hurdles faced during their
development. Discussions encompassed my strengths and areas for improvement, along with my
approach if entrusted with enhancing the college community. Leadership skills and hobbies were
also topics of exploration. My roles as PR Head for IPL Auction and in the realm of Fine Arts
with MUDRA drew their curiosity, leading to in-depth conversations. I was requested to
elucidate technical terms cited on my resume, demonstrating my familiarity with each. The
interview transitioned into my artistic influences and inspirations driving UI/UX design. When
listing my top qualities, I endeavored to align them with the company's values, encapsulating
growth, collaboration, leadership, and care.
Concluding the interview, they invited my questions, where I probed the organization's stance on
work-life balance and reduction of carbon emission. This sparked a meaningful discussion on the
organization's efforts to reduce carbon emissions, encapsulating a dynamic exchange of ideas.
Finally 8 students were selected
Invaluable Insights:

• Practice patience; my interview occurred five hours after the shortlist announcement, but

my HR interview followed just five minutes after the Technical Interview.
--- PAGE 5 ---

• Familiarize yourself with puzzles and riddles as they could be employed to evaluate your

problem-solving acumen.

• Thoroughly grasp the contents of your resume.

• Revisit Computer Science fundamentals, particularly OOPS concepts and Data Structure

algorithms.

• Devote time to comprehending DBMS concepts, with special emphasis on normalization,

Joins, Keys, and ER diagram notations.

• Ensure a comprehensive understanding of the company's core values.

• Remember that it's acceptable to admit unfamiliarity with an answer; avoid guessing and

providing incorrect information.

• Fortune does hold significance in the placement process, yet don't allow intrusive

thoughts to steer you off course.
ALL THE BEST !!! Feel free to contact me for any queries !

1. Digital Interview (Online) - All the applied students appeared for this round

This round was conducted using the HireVue Digital Interview platform. A video will narrate you the
question. Then you will get 30 seconds to 1 minute to prepare and think. Finally, you will have to answer the
question in maximum 3 minutes in only one attempt. Again, next question will be narrated through a video.
And so, there were a total of 6 questions.

The questions:

1. Why did you choose your current degree program?

2. What do you aim to gain from this internship?

4. How did you manage multiple priorities and time?

5. Tell us about a time when you realized you have a weakness and how did you try to overcome that?

6. What'd you like us to know more about you?

Tip: Be honest and give genuine answers. Do not get your answers from the internet. Be well-dressed and
give this round in a proper environment. Respond in a way that a real interviewer is sitting in front of you
because this hirevue round is manually checked, not by using AI.

2. Technical Test - 107 candidates were shortlisted for this round

Platform: Microsoft forms
Time: 30 minutes
Format: 25 MCQs
Topics Covered: DSA, SQL, Aptitude, Programming language

Tip: Don't get stuck on a question for long time. Time management is important.

3. Group Discussion - 71 students appeared for this round

There were 7 groups, each consisting of around 10 students. This round was conducted offline but the
communication medium was Microsoft teams. You are supposed to use earphones.

My experience: There were 10 students and 2 Baker Hughes Hiring team member in my panel. My GD Topic
was "ChatGPT: Pros and Cons". The GD lasted for 25 minutes. I spoke approximately 4 times, and with each
opportunity I had, I made sure to address the current status of the discussion and also added new points.
Because I added several new points my name was mentioned frequently by other students when they wanted
to add-on to my point. This kept me visible throughout the GD. 2 students were shortlisted from my group.

Tip: Adding new points to the discussion must be relevant and in context. Do not add irrelevant points just for
the sake of saying something, even few strong meaningful points gain more weightage. Do not interrupt
someone on purpose. If two students try to start a conversation at the same time (This happens quite often in a
GD, so make sure to plan out in advance what you will do in such a case) then one must politely address the
situation and ask the other to continue and may politely say that "I would like to go next after hearing your
viewpoint" or something on the similar lines. Last but not the least, have a warm smile on your face

4. Technical Interview - 28 people were interviewed in this round.

There were 3 panels set up, each panel consisting of 2 people. This round began at 10:30 am.

My experience: I had a little cold and fever that day. So, the first thing I did after entering the room was to
reduce the air conditioner cooling :/ The interviews usually go for an hour, so its better to request for the same
politely in the beginning itself if you are not well. This basically was a resume-based round. They can even
fetch out a single word from your resume and grill you on that. They first asked me to explain all the projects
mentioned in my resume. 3 projects were on Data Analytics and Machine Learning and 2 projects were on
Web development. After my brief explanation of all the projects, the next 45 minutes were questions all about
DATA. The questions ranged from Data base management system to Data analytics.
Some example question being:

1. How would you use a stationary shopkeeper's data to gain useful insights to increase his/her revenue? I had

to explain the step-by-step procedure and also mention the technical tools that will be needed to fulfil the
same.

2. How does the random forest algorithm work?

3. How do you use machine learning for classification-based problems?

4. Difference between Authentication and Authorization in context of Data base management system.

I personally have great interest in data and had explored this domain much more than what is covered in
college academics. Hence, I was able to answer all the data related questions and the interviewer was satisfied.
Then the other interviewer asked me altogether few different kind of questions. First question being, "What is
the length of the rope present on the sides of Worli Sea link bridge?". This was not a guestimate; she needed a
proper mathematical approach. This could basically be solved using the concepts of engineering mechanics
studied in the first year of engineering. I stated some terms related to tension along the rope length, rope
material, force, length of the bridge and gave a rough layout of my approach but I was afraid of concluding
my answer with an absurd number, so I just said "I will have to revise on this to get to the right number". Then
the second question was "How will you reduce the number of potholes in Mumbai?". Luckily, I had recently
watched a startup on shark tank that worked on the similar cause. I mentioned about the startup and how they
are approaching this problem and their solution.
I was also asked if given a project of some domain I am currently unaware of, will I be able to do it? What if
your friends at work are given some familiar and exciting domain project and you are stuck on some different
project? To this I answered that as a fresher what I can bring to the table is a problem-solving mindset and
good human principles. Technologies keeps on changing and updating itself very frequently, so I will be never
afraid of something unknown and give my level best to learn and complete the task assigned to me. And rather
than comparing ourselves with others, we must focus on giving our 100% and becoming better every day.
At the end, they asked me if I had any questions for them, I asked about their role in Baker Hughes and how
long have they been working at Baker Hughes. One of them was a Data Architect (hence he had asked all the
data-related question) with around 15 years of experience and the other was a Product Manager.

Tip: Do not lie on your resume. Make a good 1-page resume covering everything you know and things you
have achieved.

5. Leadership Round - 15 candidates appeared for this round

After my technical interview, I had a 10-minute break and was directly send to the conference room for the
final round with a senior director of Baker Hughes. He was associated with Baker Hughes for around 20 years.
After I introduced myself, the interview did not even feel like an interview. It was a very friendly interview,
and no typical HR questions were asked. I had spent the two years of engineering entrance exam preparation
without any coaching assistance, practicing only self-study with the help of free resources available on the
internet. He was quite impressed by that and asked me details of that journey. I talked about Sudha Murthy,
my hobbies. One question he asked me was; If I walk into your class and ask your batchmates about how you
are as a person, then what will they say? Primarily this round assesses you as a human and your thought
process.

Tip: Be honest and genuine. Do not fake anything. And again, have a warm smile on your face

All my offline rounds (GD + technical round + leadership round) had very short breaks in between and were
over by 12:30 pm. Results were out around 6pm in the evening and 8 students were shortlisted. I was one of
them!

Trust your preparation and be yourself.
Give your best and don't worry about the result.

Feel free to contact me on LinkedIn if needed. Best of luck!

The entire process consisted of five rounds spanning over a period of 1-2 weeks .

Rounds Date
Digital Interview 26 - 28 July
Technical Test 5th August
Group Discussion 7th AugustPersonal Interview
Leadership Interview

1. Digital Interview

It was a 15-minute Digital Interview on HireVue, with 6 basic HR questions about my background, choiceof Btech, weaknesses, internship expectations, and more. You have to record your answers and submitthem. The emphasis was on genuine responses, avoiding plagiarism and AI tools. After review by the HRteam, 107 students were shortlisted for the next round.

2. Technical TestThe next round was a Technical Test. It consisted of a 30-minute MCQ test on Microsoft Forms, focusingon Computer Science fundamentals and aptitude. The questions were centered around DBMS, DSA(Trees ,Graphs, sorting algorithms) , code snippets as well as quantitative aptitude. The difficulty levelranged from easy to medium. 70 students were shortlisted for the next round, which was the GroupDiscussion.

3. Group DiscussionGroup discussion was conducted virtually on microsoft teams but in college. Each group consisted ofaround 10 participants . Different topics were assigned to different groups . My group was assigned witha topic 'Generative AI'. 2 minutes were given to think about the topic and 10 minutes were given for the

discussion. Approximately 3 Students per group were selected for the next round i.e. personal interview. Total 28 students qualified for the personal interview.

4. Personal interviewThere were two interviewers. The opening question was "Tell me about yourself." I provided a briefintroduction, after which they proceeded to inquire about details from my resume. They began by askingabout each of the projects listed on my resume. I had four projects in total: one centered around theMERN Stack, another involving vanilla JavaScript, a third one implemented using JAVA and MYSQL, andthe final project being related to IoT .Ensure you have a thorough understanding of your resume beforeattending an interview as questions can cover a wide range of topics related to your resume.

Regarding the MERN project, I was asked about the authentication flow, JWT tokens, and the format ofJWT. They also asked about Firebase, which was part of my IoT project. A few students were asked towrite a code for reversing a linked list.
Next, they tested my knowledge of CCN (OSI layers), OS (linux commands) . During my introduction, Imentioned that Java is my primary programming language, hence they asked me to rate my Javaproficiency on a scale of 1 to 10 (answering between 8 and 8.5 is a good response for such questions). They also posed several questions on Object-Oriented Programming (OOPS), including questions aboutconstructors, their purpose, abstract classes, abstract methods, difference between interfaces andabstract classes.
In addition to technical questions, they also asked a few HR questions in between like strengths andweaknesses, why I want this job ? and questions related to teamwork. They also asked me about what Iknow about Baker Hughes . It's important to be prepared for questions about the company's values asthey do ask about them. Cracking this interview is easy if you are familiar with every small thing writtenon your resume. I passed this interview and reached the final round.

4. Leadership InterviewThis was essentially an HR round with a few technical questions. It was conducted with the SeniorDirector. The interviewer asked about my GD topic and my perspectives on it. As the topic was'Generative AI', she also questioned me about the various types of AI tools I am familiar with. Additionally, she presented a situation-based scenario and asked for my input and suggestions. Thetechnical questions were based on my resume. I was questioned about DBMS and database tools. Furthermore, she asked me about how communication takes place between two computers, to which Iexplained using the OSI model.

Afterward, she asked if I had any questions. It's important to ask at least one question at this stage. Ichose to ask about the types of roles I would be involved in. Confidence is key, so remember to maintaina smile on your face. Roughly 10-12 students made it to this round, and out of them, 8 students wereselected for the internship.
Few Tips :

● The placement process can be stressful, but it's important to maintain a positive attitude. Remember that everyone eventually secures a placement. Just be patient and have faith thatyou'll achieve what's destined for you. Before Baker Hughes, I hadn't been shortlisted for anyinterviews in the initial 10-12 companies. The Baker Hughes interview was my first one. So,always be prepared for every opportunity.

● Luck plays a very important role so work hard and wait for your chance.

● For the technical test, brush up your cs fundamentals. Practice coding (on leetcode) andaptitude (from indiabix, prepinsta). If you are an EXTC student ,make the most of Open Electivesubjects like DSA, DBMS, and DA .

● During a group discussion, make an effort to initiate and conclude the discussion. If you aren'tgiven the chance to start, ensure to present your points as early as you can. Don't wait forsomeone else to offer you the opportunity to speak, as that might not happen. If you remainsilent, it's over for you . Even if you contribute just two-three meaningful points, it can make adifference.

● For personal interviews, maintain confidence. Don't lie on your resume. Having knowledge of allpoints mentioned on your resume will help you clear the personal interview more easily. If youdon't remember anything , don't panic , the interviewer will help you to recall.

● Follow all the instructions given by the company and TPO. For any questions feel free to contactme on my LinkedIn : Shashank Jagtap

All the best !

Technical Tips:

• Solve a lot of DSA problems. Especially fundamental topics like Stack, Queue, Linked

List, Trees, Graphs are non-negotiable. Master these first. If you have enough time after
being comfortable with these topics, you could try and go over advanced topics like DP.

• Be familiar with Computer Science Theory like OOPS, Networking, DBMS and specific

theory of the programming language you use. If you have done some development, you
need to be familiar with its theory as well. Try to anticipate what questions could be
asked. Don't spend an ungodly amount of time on it, just go through an online crash
course or a questionnaire, it should be more than enough.

• Projects. You should be able to talk comfortably about your projects for about 10

minutes. Prepare what you are going to say beforehand and rehearse it. It constitutes a
--- PAGE 5 ---
major bulk of the interview so make sure you give enough time to it. Similar to the
previous point, try to anticipate what questions the interviewer would ask and prepare
appropriate solutions.
Interview tips:

• Be yourself.

• Before the interview try to meditate. During the interview remain calm and relaxed.

• Take pauses. Let your thoughts marinate in your head and frame sentences before

answering. Do not try to answer quickly even to questions that seem simple as you may
make a mistake in doing so. Watch this video: https://youtu.be/11EnMmH9qh4

• Always make sure you understand the question before answering, especially coding

questions. I made a similar mistake in my second interview as I mentioned above. Repeat
the question as you interpret it back to the interviewer and make sure both of you are on
the same page. Then proceed to thinking about the solution.

• Be quite stoic in your interview. Don't be too happy if you get the answer, nor too

disturbed if you don't. Take it one question at a time. Control what you can and don't
worry too much about what you cannot.

• Keep a smiling face and be very polite. More often than not people mirror each other's

body language. Sit straight and keep your spine erect. This also boosts confidence.

The placement process was divided into the following rounds:

• A preliminary coding round that consisted of 3 questions. One Easy, 2 Medium. I was

able to completely solve the first 2 problems and partially solve the last one. This was
enough to get qualified for the interview rounds.

• Technical Round 1

• Technical Round 2

• Professional Fitness Round

• HR Round

1. Technical Interview Round 1[21 Candidates appeared in this round]

The round began with the interviewer going through my resume. He asked me to give a detailed
description of the projects that I had mentioned on my resume, which I proceeded to give. He
then asked me about any challenges I faced in my projects. This took about 10-12 minutes.
He then asked me to code the famous fibonacci question. I coded up 2 solutions for the problem
and explained it in detail to him. He seemed pretty satisfied with my explanation. He then asked
me the difference between stack and queue data structures. He demanded I give an
example/application of stack and queue. This phase of the interview took 2-3 minutes.
This was followed by a series of technical questions on various computer science topics that I
had mentioned on my resume. He asked me about OOPS, polymorphism, access modifiers and
code reusability. He requested me to demonstrate these concepts. He further quizzed me about
Computer Networks, the OSI model. I was able to answer all of his questions. This part of the
interview took another 5 minutes or so.
--- PAGE 2 ---
The interviewer then proceeded to ask me a quiz question. The question is as follows: You are
given a cake and a knife. You are allowed to cut the cake 3 times only. You need to make sure that
the cake is cut in 8 pieces. I gave him the following solution: Cut the cake once, stack the 2
pieces on top of each other. Repeat this process 3 times. 1 > 2, 2 > 4, 4 > 8. He said this was a
valid solution but it would ruin the cream on the cake. A better solution would be to cut the cake
once from the top, and slice it twice through its height, resulting in 8 pieces with 3 cuts. I
admitted that his solution was better. Towards the end, we had established a decent camaraderie
and we both were smiling.
Finally, he asked me if I had any questions for him. I requested him to tell me about any project
of his, and what impact it had on an organizational level. I mentioned to him that I was really
passionate about this stuff, and therefore would love to know about it. He replied that he was not
really allowed to talk in detail about his projects but he assured me that the smallest piece of
code that one writes has an enormous impact on the organization. I was quite happy with his
response and the interview ended. It took about 20-22 minutes in total and I was selected in the
next round.

2. Technical Interview Round 2[18 Candidates appeared in this round]

In this round, the interviewer first began with a brief introduction with himself. He then asked
me to introduce myself. After my introduction, he told me to explain the projects on my resume.
After the explanation, he asked me questions about the projects. He asked me about my role in
these projects, how I collaborated with my teammates, the programming languages we used, the
API's we used, the frameworks used by us, etc. This phase of the interview lasted about 15
minutes.
The interviewer then proceeded to ask me a series of DSA questions. The following were the
questions:

• You are working at Amazon and your task is to deliver a series of packages. You are given

3 things about a delivery: The coordinates of the delivery address(x-coordinate and
y-coordinate) and the price you would get on the delivery of the package. Input is a 2d
array: [[x1,y1,p1], [x2,y2,p2], …..], with each nested array representing a delivery. The
output is a sorted input array, with the array being sorted according to the price to
distance ratio of each delivery.

• You are given an array. You need to sort the array according to the frequency of each

element in that array.

• Mirror a binary tree.

• Top view of a binary tree. You are viewing the binary tree from the top. You need to sum

all the elements that you would observe in the same line. For example if we start from the
root node, if we go to the left child and then to the subsequent right child, we would
observe the 2 nodes in the same line.
--- PAGE 3 ---
Example:
5
2 4
6
Imagine the above binary tree. In the above tree, 5, 2, 4 would be visible in the same line
if one were to view from the top.
The first 3 questions I was able to solve pretty easily. The interviewer seemed quite satisfied with
my solutions. The last question I faltered in. I did not understand the question clearly and thought
that it was a BFS question. I coded up the solution but it was not a valid one. I asked the
interviewer to explain the question to me once again, which he did again quite carefully. But,
shortly after he told me that we were out of time and he encouraged me to think about the
solution post interview.
He asked me if I had any questions for him. I asked him the same question which I had asked in
the previous interview. He was quite happy that I asked him about his projects and proceeded to
explain his projects in heavy detail. While he was speaking, subconsciously I was thinking about
the problem while simultaneously listening to him and worked up the solution mentally. Once he
was done, he asked if I could briefly attempt the solution to that problem. I explained to him the
approach and he was quite pleased with it, and told me that it was the right one.
The entire interview took about 40 minutes.

3. Professional Fitness Round

This interview began in a similar fashion as the previous interview. I was asked to introduce
myself and right after asked to explain my projects in heavy detail. The interviewer then
proceeded to ask me questions on the projects that included why certain APIs were used, and
what their purpose was. I was able to answer all his questions and the interviewer was quite
pleased with my answers. This phase took about 20 minutes.
Following was a quiz question:
You are given 2 buckets of water: one is 3 liters and the other is 5 liters. We need 4 liters of water
and cannot measure the level of water in buckets while they are partially filled.
--- PAGE 4 ---
A better explanation: https://codingnconcepts.com/puzzle/the-water-jug-riddle/
This puzzle was from a famous Die Hard movie and I was aware of this solution. I told the
interviewer that I have seen this in a movie. He smiled and challenged me to solve it immediately
which I did.
After this was a series of HR type questions. He asked me if I had an offer from abroad versus an
offer in India on my favorite tech project, which one would I choose. He asked me why I had
done a course on Financial Markets. He asked me what I wanted to accomplish in the next 5-10
years. I was able to give satisfactory responses to each question.
Similar to the first interview I managed to establish a decent rapport with the interviewer. He was
quite formal with me in the beginning but at the end he was quite comfortable discussing things
with me. I thanked him for his time and the interview ended. This round lasted for 45 minutes.

4. HR Round

This round consisted of standard HR questions, thankfully which I had gone over in my
preparation. It started with the interviewer asking for my introduction followed by these
questions:

• Why Deutsche Bank? Describe Deutsche Bank in one word.

• Describe your 2 strengths and weaknesses

• Where do you see yourself in the next 5 years?

This was followed by objective questions like family background, did I have a passport or not,
etc. This interview took 15 minutes.
