• I know this might sound cliche but do not ever think that you cannot achieve something,

self doubt kills. I lost my hope to get into DB when a month prior to placement I got the
mail that I was selected for JPMC CFG and focused primarily on web development. So
when my CFG actually got over on July 9 I had minimal days to revise my DSA concepts
as we got the news that DB was visiting the campus on July 15. I did not have the hope
that I could even clear the first round because I thought my peers were very well
prepared. But on that day I could solve 2 questions which gave me confidence that I
might get selected for the interview.

• Get your DSA skills strong. Practice questions on leetcode, gfg, codeforces anything you

like but start preparing way before the placements, in fact start doing dsa and cp from 2nd
year itself. Solving questions in the coding round requires practice which cannot be
gained overnight. I personally started doing leetcode and strivers sheet from my second
year which helped me clear the first round even if I did not do intensively 1 month before
my placements.

• Do CCN, OOPS, Java core concepts(if you have java mentioned), CCN, OS, DBMS,

SQL (Be well prepared even before the placement season starts as you may never know
when you will get selected for the interview. I had to prepare in just 5 days because I did
not have time for core subjects during june month

• Standard DSA questions are asked in the interview, start by giving the brute force and

then move to the optimal solution, this will give you time to formulate your thoughts and
give the solution with clarity.

• Do practice puzzles DB likes to ask them. Search top 20 puzzles on gig.

• Be well versed with your resume (projects and internship if any). You should know what

you have written and don't mention technologies or skills for making your resume rich.
Be honest.
--- PAGE 4 ---

• You have done an internship or not, your peers' resume looks much better- do not think

anything of that sort. I myself don't have an internship. As a fresher no one expects a lot
of things on your resume.

• Research in depth about the company- values, ethics, what services it provides, their

CEO, you should be able to answer anything. Ask questions at the end of every interview
(go only with the usual ones if you cannot think of any!).

• An interview is just like a discussion between two people and how better you can sell

yourself. Try connecting your strong points(hackathons, coding, web development) when
a question is asked and highlight them as much as possible.

• For the questions that you may not know the answer to, tell the interviewer that you do

not know this topic. It is better to say this rather than beating around the bush and giving
an unsatisfactory answer. Do not let such questions affect the rest of the interview.

• Just remember to be ready and accepting of whatever happens in the placement process.

There was one coding round and 4 interview rounds conducted. The coding round was conducted
on July 15, 2023 and the interview rounds were conducted on 26 July, 2023. The whole process
was going to be offline but only the coding round was conducted offline and the offline
interviews which were scheduled to be conducted on 20 july were postponed due to rains and the
interviews were then conducted online on 26 july.

1. Coding Round (90 mins)

The coding round was conducted on hackerearth platform. We had to go to the college to
give the test. There were 3 coding questions of 20,50,50 marks. They were two pointers,
priority queue, dp respectively. The test's duration was 90 minutes. I solved 20 marks and
one 50 marks question. 26 students were selected for interviews. But 6 students got placed
elsewhere hence got out of the interviews.

2. Technical Interview 1 (45 mins)

The interview started with the interviewer's favorite question, "Introduce yourself." The
interviewer reviewed my resume and asked about my achievements and projects. Next he
wanted to see one of the projects mentioned on my resume which was a Django project and
asked me to open the website and also told me to explain the code in the vs code. After this,
he moved on to data structures and asked me which data structures I knew about. Difference
between arrays and linked lists. What are the different sorting algorithms you know? Which
is the best among them? The best average and worst time complexity of insertion sort. What
is the requirement of binary search? What are the different layers in the OSI model? What is
the difference between router and switch? He moved on to DBMS and asked me SQL
queries. Moved on to oops concepts- difference between abstraction and encapsulation.
Difference between java overriding and overloading. Is overriding static polymorphism?
What are the different access modifiers in java? Furthermore, he asked about the various
--- PAGE 2 ---
access modifiers in Java and whether a private class can be inherited, and if so, which access
modifiers are allowed for the child class. The interviewer then wanted to move on to actual
coding- so I have an array with positive and negative numbers in it and you have to pair up
positive numbers from it such that when you add them up then the corresponding negative
number should be present in the array. The interviewer was impressed with my reasoning and
quick responses and decided to end the interview here. I then asked him a couple of
questions.
18 students were selected from 20 students.

3. Technical Interview 2 (45 mins)

The interview started with the usual "introduce yourself." The interviewer asked about my
two favorite projects from the resume, and we had a good discussion about them. Then, he
asked about the Code for Good hackathon and wanted an explanation about it. Moving on to
coding questions, he asked about Huffman coding, to which I honestly admitted that I didn't
know the algorithm. He then asked about minimum spanning trees and explained Kruskal's
algorithm. Next, he asked me to find the middle element in a linked list. He then gave me
some questions to solve in my IDE. One of which was→ Consider a circular array and find a
subarray of size k with maximum. In the DBMS section, he asked about different
normalization forms and asked about serializable schedules. He then asked me questions on
java and oops concepts. How can we achieve abstraction? What is interface and abstract
classes, state the differences. Can an interface be private? Or any of its methods? Difference
between static and final keywords? Can static methods be overridden? The interviewer
presented a puzzle involving three switches and three bulbs, which is a famous one from
GFG.
https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/puzzle-7-3-bulbs-and-3-switches/
Now he had no further questions for me as I had answered everything. He asked me if I knew
about guesstimates. I acknowledged that I was aware of them but unsure about how to
approach them. He proceeded to give me a question, asking me to determine the number of
cars in the evening in Andheri. I attempted to approach it, but unfortunately, I couldn't figure
it out so he guided me on how to approach it. Towards the end, he asked if I had any
questions, and I asked a few. Around 13 students were selected for the profit round.

4. Professional fitness round (30 minutes)

The interviewer directly asked situational and behavioral questions. For example, how would
I react if a project I worked on had issues with the model, and everyone blamed me? If the
issue escalated to the manager, how would I handle it? If you are put into a team which has a
completely different tech stack what will you do? If for this reason your team lacks behind
because you were taking time to complete it how will you take responsibility for it? If a
member of your team now complains about it how will you react? etc. They also asked about
--- PAGE 3 ---
my strengths and why I wanted to join Deutsche Bank. They inquired if I would reject an
offer from another banking company for DB. Finally, they asked if I had any questions. In the
end, 10 students were selected for the HR round.

5. Hr round (30 minutes)

This was a standard HR Round. Tell me something about yourself? Minimal questions were
asked on DB Values and ethics. What is the biggest challenge you faced till now? Gave me
situational questions on how you would handle the situation if your team contains lazy
people who are not contributing to the project. Now your manager is upset with all of you.
How will you handle it? This went pretty well so he decided to end it and asked me if I had
any questions?
Verdict: Selected :) All 10 students were selected

questions on linked list (find middle element, delete nth last element) He then asked about
different searching techniques (linear & binary), their time and space complexity, different
sorting algorithms, their complexities.
He next asked about java concepts like polymorphism, overloading, overriding with examples
and access modifiers in java. He asked if private methods can be inherited, he then asked what
can be the access modifiers of overridden methods in child class. I said that child class needs to
have equal or broader access than parent class and not be more restrictive than parent class to
which he asked if I am sure. I said yes and so he asked me to google it later and said he too
would google it.
Then he asked a tweaked version of the famous two sum problem. I gave the brute force
solution, then optimised one with hashset, which he was not satisfied with so I gave another two
pointer optimised approach with the time complexity of all methods. He asked me to code the
pseudo code on my local editor. He was satisfied with my answer. I asked him a few questions
and the interview ended.

3. Technical Interview 2 (1hr)

The interviewer jumped right into my resume and asked about my internship. We discussed my
work in depth.
The interviewer asked about each of my project in depth. My first project used ML so we
discussed in depth about the algorithm, like why I had chosen that particular algo (CNN), what
are other different types of CNN, which one I used. He asked if I could improve the accuracy of
my model, could the accuracy be 100%? If yes, how. If no, why not etc. He asked in depth about
the internal working of my second project, the behaviour of my website and about APIS. He also
asked about MVC. He grilled a lot about minute details but also was helpful.
--- PAGE 2 ---
He then asked me DBMS concepts and a few SQL queries. We then discussed databases and case
scenarios when to use which and concepts about different types of databases. He then asked a dsa
question. It was tweak of a leetcode problem
(https://leetcode.com/problems/search-in-rotated-sorted-array/). I gave the brute force solution
followed by the optimised approach. He asked me to write the pseudo code of the optimised
solution on my IDE. He was satisfied with my answer.
I asked him a question which he asked if TPO told us to ask them as everyone had been asking
him the same question.

4. Profit round (20 mins)

This was a chill round. The interviewer remembered me from the ppt session as I had asked a
question. He asked hr questions like who is my role model, my most interesting project and
inspiration etc. He also asked a few situational and behaviourial questions like how I have
averted a crisis etc.
I asked him 2 questions about which we discussed for quite some time and the interview ended
on a very positive note.

5. HR round (20 mins)

This started with my introduction, followed by situational and behaviourial questions like when
have I showcased leadership etc. He then asked about my internship and what I learnt from there,
why would I join an investment bank over a tech company, why DB over that company, what if
another company offers me more salary than DB etc. The key is to always choose DB with a
convincing answer. For example - apart from monetary compensation, a company provides
experience and growth which at DB would be more fruitful than at some other company. Never
speak ill of another company, instead focus on why you would go for DB (their values, culture,
growth etc.) He also asked about family background and other general stuff.

Useful Tips:

1. Prepare CS fundamentals thoroughly (OS, CN, DBMS) and practice as much DSA as

possible (Leetcode).

2. It is luck based. Your interviewer will ask what they prepared/are expert in so be ready for

anything.

3. If you get rejected in the last 2 rounds, dont worry it was hard luck...you are technically

well prepared, but focus on how confident you sound while speaking and always be
positive while giving answers. Even if you dont know any answer, say so directly and dont
get disheartened by it throughout the interview.

4. Asking questions during the PPT and interviews is necessary but ask good questions. Dont

just ask interviewers about their project and experience in that company, techstack or other
cliche questions.
All the best!!

journey.prep:
1. Read the JD thoroughly. Always try to align your resume with the skills required(Though it doesn't matter

if your resume is technical or non-technical for this role). Do talk with your seniors in the same domain. Try
to gather as much information as you can. I also talked with a couple of my CA friends about this role and
how to prepare for the same.

2. Read your resume and be completely honest in your answers. The interviewers are experienced enough to

gauge your understanding of the stuff put up in the resume. Make sure you know each and every word you
put on your resume.

3. Even if you have a basic understanding of finance and risk terms it would be okay. you should be able to

deviate your interview based on your top skills. Also learn about the role and try to do any course if you
have some time before the interview day. It will greatly help you.

4. Do prepare 1-2 good questions to ask at the end of the interview. But do keep in mind don't ask too many

open-ended questions because they too don't want to feel that they are being interviewed.

5. Learn from the mistakes you have made in the past interviews and work on them.

6. Ensure that you speak in a coherent and calm manner to sound formal. The interviewers want to know

what you've got for them to consider you. Make the most of your time.

HR round but were not short-listed and trust me that's the worst feeling when you can see the finish line but
you were not able to make it.

know or remember.

1. Resume Screening

The actual process of JPMC started with the 1st company itself (Application date: 8th July). They asked to
apply for the role in Gform as well as their portal. In this round screening was done based on the resumes.
Therefore, It is important to have a strong, if not excellent, resume that includes your skills,
extracurricular activities, GPA, projects, internships, and other relevant information. The resume
was a talking point during my interviews.
11th July shortlisted candidates names were released.
82 Students were shortlisted.

2. Online Aptitude Test(12th July)

There was an extra round this time. It was an aptitude test which had 29 questions and we had 45 mins. Most
of the questions were on CAT Quantitative analysis. Make sure to practice those beforehand and also try to
use more and more tricks to save time in the exam. Also the questions are almost Quant/ CAT level.
Results of this round were a bit delayed. Results were declared on 18th July.
28 Students were shortlisted.
There was a PPT for the selected candidates(On Zoom). Be active during these rounds, make notes about
companies requirements, tech stack being used, any specific condition and skills they are looking for, make
sure to ask good questions. (But it doesn't affect much)

3. Business Round 1(26 Students appeared- 2 got selected for different company)

The interviews started around 10.00 -10.30 am. The interviewer went through my resume simultaneously
and asked me questions related to my internships, positions of responsibilities, extra curricular activities in
--- PAGE 2 ---
detail. Therefore, ensure that you are completely thorough with every single word mentioned in your
resume. Few questions that I recall are:

1. Thad mentioned Design thinking as one of my courseworks so she asked phases of Design thinking

2. Then she asked which language I am proficient in? (Java) So she asked why Java and why not

Python? She just wanted to know what I thought before deciding on anything.

3. Then she asked me to explain one of my projects in depth. Also she asked me how I could monetize

this project.

4. Then she went on asking me situational questions like as I was team leader in one of the hackathon

which we won. Like what were the challenges I faced, how I solved them. Also like if 2 team players
are not performing to fullest what will I do? If there is conflict in the team what will I do?

5. Then she asked me about my weaknesses and how I improved on them?

6. Then she asked me why finance and why non-tech?

7. She asked me do I have any idea or opinion on current global scenario of international markets? I did

had some idea but sooner I did hit a deadend because I wasn't aware of a recent incident in depth.

8. She asked me about risk management in general, what is risk and what are it's stages and phases etc.

9. Then at last she asked me do I have any questions for her? (Response: Nothing as such specific but

still I do wanna know what's the one piece of advice would you like to give me if I want to succeed
in this role if I get selected)
The interview lasted for about 35-40 minutes, however, for some it was only 15-20 minutes.
> 15 students were shortlisted for the second interview

4. Business Round 2 (15 Students appeared for this round)

This was same as the first round but some of my friends had a panelist which was pure technical so do
prepare for both scenarios. There were 2 interviewers. They asked me questions related risk and types of
risks and risk management in general. It is important to note that if you're unable to answer any question,
just acknowledge that you don't know. Then one of the panelist asked me to take any one project which I
like and start explaining it in and out and how you thought about this project how you worked on it and how
you convinced your mentor to work on this project. He gave me hypothetical situation that if my mentor is
not aligned with my views then how will I convince him/her? Then if I had conflict in my team how will I
resolve it? Then if I was given a project of which I had no idea then will I take that project and given ample
time will I do it? (Yes provided I had to do it anyhow) Then he asked me if you had an option of doing alone
or with team what will i choose?(Obv team over myself because if same task can be done within 2-3 months
then why not) Then he asked but teams have conflicts why would you want conflict if you simply can avoid
by doing yourself? So this is how he was trying to make me fall in this trap of questions. So do have a firm
belief about things as well as try to make your point and stick to it. This was done deliberately by the
interviewer to see how my I will react in these situations. So stay calm and make your point clear.
Finally, they'll ask if you have any questions for them(I asked the same question which I asked in Round 1).
This interview lasted for about 20-30 minutes.

3. HR Round (7 Students appeared for this round)

Almost immediately after the 2nd interview I was called for the HR Round. This was a very casual
conversational type round wherein you will be generally asked about location preference, if I was
comfortable working late nights. Why JPMC and why this risk management role? Why should we hire you
and not the 28 others that we interviewed? Then at last do I had any questions for them?(To which I replied
that nothing as such relevant because I had been asking questions in these last 2 rounds and I am pretty
--- PAGE 3 ---
much clear about the company as well as this role). So it doesn't matter what you ask or not it's just a basic
courtesy to ask a question but it is not a deciding factor for your selection.
5 Students were offered the Job.

journey.prep:
Panelists' preferences and questioning styles can differ, so I suggest getting ready for a wide range of
questions. These might relate to your resume, the job role, or even general situational queries. Keep in
mind that these interviewers were once engineering students themselves, just like we are now. They
possess extensive knowledge about technology, so it's best to avoid trying to deceive them or providing
incomplete answers. They'll likely recognize it.

Around 14-15 students were shortlisted for the next round

4. Interview Round 2

The second round consisted of a technical assessment with two panelists. Af ter their introductions,
they immediately launched into questioning without asking me for an introduction. One panelist
initiated the session by inquiring about my preference for JPMC and what motivated me to pursue the
role. Additionally, they inquired ab out the CEO and CFO of JPMC, to which I could only respond
with the CEO's name.
The second panelist then delved into technical matters. Initially, they inquired about the technologies
I had mentioned in one of my projects, such as Cloud Services and AI to ols. They wanted to know
why I chose these technologies and their significance within the project. The discussion shifted to my
Machine Learning project, where I provided a brief explanation. Subsequently, the focus shifted to
Object-Oriented Programming ( OOPS) concepts, where I was prompted to present code examples
illustrating the four pillars of OOPS.
The technical assessment then turned to a SQL query task, where I was asked to formulate a query to
retrieve the second -highest salary from an employee ta ble. The panelist circled back to my resume,
noticing that I had mentioned Flask as my preferred backend framework. They requested that I create
an HTML form, explaining that upon clicking a button, the entered details should be stored in a
database using Flask. I proceeded to write the complete code, elaborating on each step and clarifying
the code's functionality. The panelist seemed satisfied with my approach and concluded their technical
inquiries.

Towards the conclusion, the other panelist inquired about my strengths and weaknesses, and how these
traits would impact my work at JPMC. With these questions answered, my second interview came to

an end. They also provided an opportunity for me to ask questions. I inquired about their tech stack
and whether t hey regularly adopt new versions or tools.  The entire technical assessment lasted
approximately one hour.

Useful Tips-

For technical round like these, you need to understand what role the company is offering and prepare
accordingly. There wasn't any DSA involved but it might have been the case if the role was SDE. So,
prepare according to the role. Bu t, nevertheless, always know what you've included in your resume
and be ready to answer those questions.

7 students were shortlisted for 3rd round

5. Interview Round 3 (HR Round)

Following the second round , the transition to the HR round was swift. The atmosphere during this
discussion was quite informal, and the questions posed were of a general nature. The topics included
my reasons for selecting the CR role and specifically JPMC as the pref erred choice. Additionally, I
was asked to clarify why I was seeking an internship at JPMC, considering that other companies like
PhonePe were offering internships coupled with pre-placement offers (I+P) at our college.

The HR representative also inquired about my comprehension of the role's responsibilities and whether
I would be comfortable with potential day shifts or night shifts if required. This round reached its
conclusion within a mere 10 minutes.

At the end, 5 students were offered the internship with me being one of them.

Useful Tips:

1. Carefully go through the job description (JD). Match your resume with the needed skills, whether it's

technical or non-technical. Talk to seniors in the same field and gather information. Consulting friends
in related domains, like financially sounded friends in my case, can be helpful too.

2. Familiarize yourself with your resume and give honest answers. Interviewers can sense your

understanding of what you've mentioned. Know every detail on your resume.

3. Basic knowledge of finance and risk terms suffices. Lead the interview w ith your strongest skills. If

possible, take a small course before the interview for better preparation.

4. Prepare a few thoughtful questions to ask at the end. Avoid too many open -ended questions, as you

don't want the interviewers to feel interviewed.

5. Learn from past interview mistakes and improve upon them.

6. Speak confidently and coherently to come across as formal. Use your time effectively to showcase

your strengths.

7. Be well-prepared for HR questions. A strong HR round is crucial for moving forward.

8. Familiarize yourself with J.P. Morgan and Chase's values and activities. If asked, share what you know.

9. Approach the interview with a clear mindset. Your clarity of thought and humble, sharp demeanor

matter.

Best of luck for your interviews! Stay positive during the placement process. Interviews are as much as
they are about you as a person as they are about skills or achievements. If any queries, you can easliy find
me on LinkedIn.

understanding.

management.

shifts. Towards the end, he asked me to specify which divisio n I would prefer to work in, as JPMC
was offering roles in middle office, risk reporting, and project risk management for the Corporate Risk
position.

interview lasted about 20-25 minutes.

Each round is an elimination round. Round 2 was on the 13th of July
2023(online) and the rest of the rounds took place on the 21st of July 2023(offline).
List of rounds:

1. Resume Screening

2. Aptitude Test

3. Group Discussion

4. Interview Round 1

5. Interview Round 2

6. HR Round

ROUND 1: Resume Screening

o In this round, the company scanned all the resumes and sent the shortlist to college. My
suggestion would be to keep 2 copies of resume in hand, one to be attached while sending
to company and second carried on campus.
o Always use a Latex resume to be sent in online screening tests.
o Keep your resume very clear and to the point. Do not put anything that you are not aware
of or are dicey. Make sure that it contains key words related to banking and finance.
70 students were shortlisted for the aptitude test.

ROUND 2: Aptitude Test (70 applicants)

o This round was completely online, that is it was not mandatory to stay on campus while
attempting the test.
o There was a window of 30 minutes (1p.m to 1.30 pm) to log in to the test. The round
comprised 45 questions for 45 minutes, 10 on Market Awareness (Questions on current
affairs), 10 on Corporate Finance (Basics of Accounting and Financial Ratios), 15 on
Quantitative Aptitude and 10 on Verbal Reasoning.
o The questions on Verbal and market awareness were easy and quants and finance between
easy to moderate. Overall, it was moderate exam. The catch here was the time limit per
question.
Out of 70, 59 students were shortlisted for the round.

ROUND 3: Group discussion (59 students)

o Every year the company keeps a banking workshop, but for my batch they had kept group
discussion. Initially the topic was not disclosed.
o I had prepared on various topics, like diversity, inclusion, G20 mission, technology. Make
sure to be ready in case topic is not disclosed.
o 2 days before the interview, late night we received the topic "Current trends in banking
system in India and across the globe."
o The discussion lasted for 20-25min in groups on 10. There were 2 interviewers present who
were giving inputs and giving us topics to talk on. Be active and respond politely. Make
sure to add new and innovative points so that panellists notice you. Keep yourself updated
with recent market news.
o We were allowed to carry mobile phones and refer the points we have noted down, but it
may not be the case for your batch. So be ready to speak without reference.
o There are some ground rules for group discussion, make sure you always follow them.
From my panel, 5 of us were sent for next round and from 59 students in total 35 students were
shortlisted.

ROUND 4: Interview Round 1

o The shortlisted candidates were divided into 8 panels, each had 1 or 2 members from the
recruitment team.
o The round began with very normal conversation; they try to calm you down. My
interviewer asked me to introduce myself. By that time, he was scanning through my
resume. He caught on the minors in management course from SPJIMR. He started asking
me how exactly the selection is done, what were the topics covered. After 10-15 min he
moved on to the finance questions.
o Initially, he asked me what is accounting and what was my understanding on it. I explained
him in detail 3 financial statements. He then moved on to asking how the statements were
linked to each other. The next question came that how was revenue recognized. At this point
I got confused so I asked him to elaborate a bit. I then answered the concept of accrual and
cash basis. I also explained him revenue recognition criteria.
o He saw in my resume a project that I had done in core finance which interested him very
much. There was a detailed round of questioning that took place on the project. He also
gave me suggestions to improve it further. Overall, this project was the key which helped
me in further rounds.
o We then moved on to the puzzles and quick maths. He asked me a probability puzzle from
GFG which I could not recollect at that moment.  I told him how much I could recall and
then he gave me a few hints as well. After 5-7 min of trying, I gave up and told him I am
unable to solve. For this question use of paper allowed. He then asked 67 ✕ 73 mentally to
which I gave him the approach and the correct answer. Note that none of the mental maths
such as squares, square root question allows the use of calculator.
o At the end, the interviewer asked me my future plans. He was very blunt in asking are you
planning to give CAT this year to which I answered no.
o The interview lasted for more than 45min.
o In any of the questions, be it quick maths, puzzles, or finance, do not pause for 1-2 min.
Rather walk him through your approach and simultaneously keep calculating. It is your
attitude to attempt the questions rather than the answer.
o Make sure to be very through with core financial concepts and basics.
o After this round, we lost track of how many applicants were shortlisted for the next rounds
as the rest of the rounds were conducted in parallel.

I was shortlisted was both, CIB, and CR roles, so my interviews were going on in parallel.
However, for the CIB role my round 2 was not taken and I was sent directly for HR Round.
Only 2 candidates out of the selected ones had this opportunity to go directly by skipping one
round.

ROUND 5: HR Round

o This was the final round. I was greeted at the beginning by a panel only one lady. It started
with how are you, how was your day.
o The she moved on to my family background and asked me a few questions on it. I
mentioned that my father works in a CA firm, so she asked my why not CA then, why
MBA. This was a partial trick question because she wanted to see how I justified my reason
for choosing a particular career field.
o She then asked me to talk about something which was not there my resume. Fortunately, I
had not put my college projects in the resume, so I spoke in details about the Sem 4, Sem
6 and current major project. Mention any significant progress that you have made in this
project. I mentioned filing a patent on the project.
o She then asked me why JPMC and what I expected from the role. I was asked 2-3 times
why I wanted to work in Investment Banking and not in Corporate Risk. I talked about my
passion and liking. She also asked me why I did not try for Fintech.
o In the end, I was asked whether I had any questions. I asked her 2 questions. (Keep a few
questions ready beforehand)
o The round lasted for 15 - 20 min.
In total, 13 students were selected for the internship.

Important Points to Note:
 This link has all the resources I used for the preparation.
https://drive.google.com/file/d/1Nwf3VM4tBb92TxsgUxDtghXyLeSLHU_v/view?usp=s
haring   (Please open on laptop / desktop)
 It is a pure non-technical finance role and we as engineering students come from a very
strong technical background, so they do not expect you to know a lot about finance and
accounting (do not take this lightly). However, having a few courses such as Accounting
Fundamentals, Corporate Finance from CFI would help you stand out from others. It
personally helped me a lot so I highly recommend you to do this course or any other
equivalent course. Apart from CFI, you may refer to Investopedia.
 Study the current affairs such as merger and acquisition deals, Market trends and IPO
launches from Economic Times. Read the past 1month news in detail. Make sure you are
aware about topics like SENSEX, NIFTY, GDP. They just want to check how aware you
are of things going on in the domain that you aspire to work in.
 While solving the mental math questions and puzzles keep explaining your approach, do
not pause for more than a minute if in case required for calculations. It is okay not to get
the correct answer, but the attempt carries brownie points.
 The interviewers try to test your personality in every interview, so work on your
communication skills, and confidence and never go blank for any question, if you don't
know the answer just explain your thought process. Keep smiling throughout and always
maintain eye contact with the panellists.
 Be very honest while creating your resume and while giving the interview. Do not give
them any chance to grill over something that you've mentioned on the resume and is not
true. Be thorough with your resume. Prepare detailed answers on every section of your
resume. Start from introduction, move on to the education. If you have taken up minors, be
ready to answer that as well. Create a sample answer format for projects, internships,
achievements and even certificate sections. I will attach a few common questions that can
possibly be asked on resume sections.
 Do not wait for the placement season to commence to start your preparations. Believe me,
you will not get any time once the season starts, so be prepared well in advance. I myself
had started preparing a year ago, and this was the point that the interviewers liked a lot.
 Be prepared for questions like, "Where do you see yourself in 5 years?", "Do you have any
plans for higher studies?" or "Why won't you consider MBA as an option as it would add
more value to your resume?" while answering such questions do not mention your higher
studies plans although you may have one. I will also try to attach as many HR Questions
as possible.
 Placement season is extremely stressful, so stay physically, mentally and emotionally
strong during the process. Do not believe any rumours regarding the companies not arriving
the campus, the TPO will officially keep sending updates regarding the companies and the
roles offered.
 Feel free to reach out to the seniors in case of any doubts regarding the placement process
or any role-specific questions, we are here for y'all. Also, in case of any doubts for the CIB
or CR roles, you can definitely reach out to me or connect on LinkedIn.
 Lastly, stay calm and composed during the process. Be enthusiastic while answering the
questions. The company is always looking forward to work with people who are passionate
and active, so make sure you deliver that. Do not panic!
All The Best Guys!
You've Got This :))

For the placement process, three rounds were conducted. There was a resume shortlisting round before any
of the actual rounds happened. 112 students were shortlisted after the resume round.

1. Round 1: SQL Round

Around 40 students had applied for the role of a data analyst. Round 1 was the SQL round. I was
interviewed by a panel of two full timers. The questions were straightforward and ranged from very easy to
hard leetcode SQL queries. The interviewers increased the level of questions after each correct answer. I
was asked 4 questions in this round. The first question was a simple where query. The second question was
a simple join query. The third question was that of sorting the table. I gave two approaches for the third
question. The first approach had a small error so I was asked to find the error and rectify it. The second
approach was correct. The fourth question was a follow-up question of the third one and it was a complex
query so the interviewer asked me to explain the approach and not write it down. After which the
interviewer explained the correct logic for this question. The interview went on for 30 minutes.

2. Round 2: SQL + Guestimates

The second round was a longer round. It went on for about an hour. 10 students were shortlisted for this
round. I was asked to introduce myself again. Then a google spreadsheet was shared with me which
contained the schema for two tables followed by 7 questions. I was given 15 minutes to solve those 7
questions. Level of the questions was medium and hard leetcode queries. I was able to solve 5 questions
and started with the 6th one but time was up. After that the interviewer asked me to find an error and rectify
it which I had made in the first query. He then asked me the approach for the other two queries which I
hadn't solved. I was able to answer one but I didn't know the approach to the second one so I told him.
We then moved on to guestimates. The first question that was asked was to estimate the number of bank
accounts present for a particular bank. The second question was to estimate the number of tea cups
consumed in Delhi throughout the month. The third question was to estimate the number of people living in
a housing society. I gave a straightforward answer for this one where I took the average family size per
household multiplied by the average houses on a floor multiplied by the number of floors. However the
interviewer wanted me to take into account the varying sizes of household and asked me to think
--- PAGE 2 ---
accordingly. I proceeded by assuming that each house on a floor houses a different number of people based
on the size of the house. He then asked if I has any questions for them.

3. Round 3: HR/Culture Fit

This round was a 30 minute round. 4 students were shortlisted for this round. The interviewer was an SPIT
alumni. He started off by introducing himself. Then he asked for my introduction. He then shared his
college experience and some valuable insights. He asked me the same questions regarding my college
experience till date. Then he asked me about my extracurricular activities and the committees I was a part
of. He asked me my highest point of life till date and to give reasons for the same. Then he asked me my
lowest point and we had a little chat about that. Finally he asked me if I had any questions for him.
2 students were given the job including me. Keep in mind that the interviewer tests you right from the
beginning as soon as he starts chatting with you about his college life etc. Don't get carried away and end
up saying something you don't mean to. This round mainly checks your behavior with other colleagues and
your ability to communicate properly with utmost clarity.

The placement process involved three rounds, preceded by a pre-placement talk and resume shortlisting. The
pre-placement talk allowed candidates to ask questions and learn about the company. After the resume
shortlisting, 113 students proceeded to further rounds.

1. Round 1 (SQL Round) [ 40 students appeared for this round ]

The interview session lasted for approximately 30 minutes. It began with me introducing myself and making
sure to present myself well while mentioning my strengths. Following that, I was prompted to assess my
proficiency in SQL on a scale of 1 to 5. I rated myself a 4, reserving 1 point for potential improvement.
Subsequently, I was presented with an employee database schema and tasked with executing straightforward
queries. These queries encompassed tasks such as sorting, identifying unique values, and gradually
increased in complexity with each subsequent question. The SQL-related questions posed during the
interview were of intermediate difficulty and spanned various concepts including aggregate functions,
joins, and the 'group by' clause etc Furthermore, the interview included several theoretical questions
pertaining to DBMS theory, encompassing topics such as data types, DDL, DML, cross join,
distinctions between cross join and right join, and the applications of partition keys. I provided accurate
responses to these questions, leading to a discussion about the projects listed on my resume. Given the role's
focus on data, I highlighted relevant projects on data analysis, data engineering, and machine learning
domain. This served to underscore my keen interest in the realm of data. Just so you know, the interview was
done online using the Gmeet platform and I was asked to share my screen and write queries on Notepad.
Total 10 students were shortlisted for further rounds.

2. Round 2 Problem Solving Round] [ 10 students appeared for this round]

The interview extended for about an hour and was conducted by the Product Lead at WorkIndia. Unlike
past years interview experiences, I wasn't asked any guesstimate questions. The interview began with me
introducing myself once again. To demonstrate my keen interest in the data field, I mentioned that I had
undertaken projects in different domains such as data engineering, data science, and data analysis. I was
--- PAGE 2 ---
then asked several questions related to my projects. Following this, the interviewer inquired about the
app I used most frequently on my mobile. I replied that it was WhatsApp. He followed up by asking
about the latest feature I had observed on WhatsApp, to which I answered "WhatsApp Digital
Payments." This shift in the interview's direction led to discussions about product-related scenarios,
essentially testing my ability to approach and assess features. We delved into topics such as evaluating
feature success through data analysis, particularly in the context of WhatsApp Digital Payments. The
conversation covered various cases, including entering a market with strong competitors, tracking
feature success over time, and comparisons with other competitors. The interviewer used these
questions to gauge my logical thinking, problem-solving abilities, and my approach to conducting
data analysis and product feature analysis. Continuing with the interview, I was presented with an
Instagram database schema. My task was to write queries for tracking user engagement with
different features on Instagram. These queries were quite challenging and tested my
understanding of self joins, subqueries, and timestamp-related queries. After correctly addressing
them, I was given a puzzle to solve. I managed to solve it accurately, and the interviewer probed into my
approach for arriving at the solution. Throughout the interview, the interviewer consistently assessed my
thought processes and approaches in solving various cases and questions. It was crucial to effectively
communicate each approach to ensure clarity. In essence, the interview highlighted the importance of
demonstrating clear approaches and problem-solving techniques, especially in the context of analyzing
product features. Later in the interview, I was given the chance to ask the interviewer any questions I
had. This moment provides an opportunity to set yourself apart from other candidates. Instead of asking
common questions, it's important to conduct research about the company's work. By posing distinctive
questions, you can make a memorable impression. Inquiring about unique and different aspects
demonstrates your genuine interest in the company. Further 3 students were selected for the final round
including me.

3. Round 3 (Culture Fit Round) [ 3 students appeared for this round]

The round commenced at 6:30 pm in the evening and spanned around 45 to 50 minutes. The interviewer,
a co-founder and alumnus of SPIT, began by introducing himself. I followed suit with my introduction,

your problem-solving abilities.

in mock interviews helps you identify areas for improvement, work on your delivery, and build the
stamina needed for actual interviews.

journey.prep:
• Aptitude Test: Indiabix and similar websites can be helpful to get you started with the type of

questions. But the difficulty level is higher on the test and hence you should solve more questions at
approximately CAT level. And also being mindful of the time for each section is crucial.

• For guesstimates and other case studies, one of the best channels to get started with is 'Case

Interviews Cracked'. For more preparation you should ideally practice with your friends and switch
between interviewer and interviewee. And also give feedback after each session to understand your
weaknesses. Pick up some questions from the internet and try making the session as close to the real
thing as possible.

• Resume: You need to know everything that's on your resume and you need to be thorough with it.

This is very essential.

• Try finding out the most common HR type questions and have answers ready for the same. Having at

least a basic frame of what you want to say will help you remember when you actually have to
answer them.

• Most of the interview regarding guesstimates and case studies is mainly based on how well you're

structured and how well you can explore the given question. The calculations matter less than your
approach, so if you think your number may be wrong, just mention it to the interviewer and proceed
further. So, keep practicing and you'll get the hang of the basic frameworks for each type and you
can infer more knowledge as you go further in the question.

• The people taking the interview were very relaxed and it was comfortable to talk to them while

giving the interview. If you do start to think you're stuck or you're panicking, just tell them that you
want a minute or two and calm down and proceed at your own pace.

• One last important thing is to pay attention during the pre-placement talk and understand what the

company does and research more about the company on your own time. Questions about how much
you know about the company always come up in any interview for any company.
You can approach and contact me on LinkedIn at any time. I'd be happy to answer all your questions.
All the best for your placements!!

1. Aptitude Round: ~100 Students

The first round consisted of an Aptitude Test of 60 mins where it was divided into Attention to Detail,
Quantitative, Data Interpretation, Logical Reasoning, Verbal Reasoning and Abstract Reasoning. All the
sections were timed and you could only attempt each section once and no navigation between the sections
while a particular section was being solved was allowed.
The questions were at a higher level than normal aptitude tests have. Indiabix will not be enough to prepare
for these. There was no negative marking.
37 Students were selected for interview rounds.

2. Interview Round 1: (~30 mins)

The interview process started by the interviewer asking me how I was doing and to tell me about myself.
Then he asked me about why do you want to do consultancy, tell me how you are a team player(as I had
mentioned this on my resume). Next he asked me about a solution for my father's business that has helped
the company (I mentioned to him that my father has a business and I have had exposure to the business
side). He also asked about my plans for higher studies. Next he proceeded with a guesstimate "Calculate the
number of planes in Indian airspace at any given moment". At the end of the interview I asked him a couple
of questions about the company and about the skills to learn if I do get selected.
22 people were shortlisted further.

3. Interview Round 2: (~25 mins)

The interview started just 15 mins after I was done with round 1. The interviewer introduced themselves and
what they do in the company. First question asked to me was what was my motivation to do consulting.
Further she asked why GEP and also why consulting. Then she asked what I thought the role of a consultant
is. Then she asked me what procurement and supply chain means (as I had mentioned previously when
talking about the company). She then asked me about the project I had mentioned in the resume and
following that she asked to list challenges faced, solutions found and the outcome realized during the term of
the project. Then we moved on to a guesstimate "Calculate the total number of people traveling in a day
from Mumbai to Delhi on Indigo flights". I went on with guesstimate while confirming my steps with the
--- PAGE 2 ---
interviewer and finished until she was satisfied with the answer. Lastly she asked me why I wanted to go
into a non tech domain.
About 8 people were shortlisted further.

4. Interview Round 3: (~25 mins)

The interview was conducted in the TPO office. The interviewer started with him introducing himself and
then asked to introduce myself to him. He started by asking about my project and some details around it. He
then asked me a puzzle about the Two wires problem. Then he asked me about what I knew about GEP.
Then he moved on to a profitability question "Your client is a travel agency and they have been seeing less
profits than the industry average. Analyze the issue.' I approached the question as a usual profitability
question and used the basic framework. After discussing multiple sectors and factors, I was stuck with what
the actual issue that the company was facing. He then proceeded to give the actual answer to what was the
issue and what could be the reason it was happening.
Finally, 4 people were offered the job. (All from S.P.I.T.)

The selection process consisted a total of 4 rounds: OA + 2 Technical + HR.
The OA consisted of 12 MCQ-type questions on core concepts such as OOPS, DBMS, and even some Java
based questions. The MCQs in and of themselves should not be difficult given you have paid some amount
of attention in the college lectures. Some quick brushup from GFG, Interviewbit would do the job just fine
for the MCQs.
Next the coding question: this was a variation of leetcode medium question:
https://leetcode.com/problems/number-of-islands/description/
The twist was that instead of 1s and Os, there were 4 different characters(a,b,c,d). I was able to pass all test
cases with a simple BFS approach, as I had done this question previously.

1. Technical 1 [ 49 candidates selected for Tech 1]

The interview started with the usual question: "Tell me about yourself." My suggestion would be to
prepare a good response to this question, unlike me. He then turned to my resume, from which the
interviewer asked me about my projects. Be sure you are thoroughly aware of the things you have done in
ALL of your projects. Don't mention the projects you are unsure about, or haven't done much work on. He
asked me quite a few questions about my 'favourite project". After this, he turned to some DSA questions.
The difficulty of these was not too high, would say about easy-medium in leetcode. Solving medium
questions on leetcode would get you through these. He also asked me a very simple SQL query to "find the
3rd greatest salary from emp table". After this, he asked me some core concept questions on OOPS, DBMS.
This round lasted for about 40-45 minutes.

2. Technical 2 [Around 20-30 candidates]

Started, with the same "Tell me about yourself" question, followed by "What do you know about
MSCI?" After this, the interviewer told me to write code to find the index of the first occurring "1" in a
sorted array of 1s and Os. I first answered with a simple linear search, and then after asking to optimize it, a
binary search. She then proceeded with my resume and asked which language I preferred to code in and
why. After which she asked me some questions about my summer internship and why wouldn't I be
continuing with the same company. Finally, she gave a logical reasoning question to solve, on a sheet of
paper. These types of questions can be found on GFG, interviewbit, etc very easily.
Lasted for about 30-35 minutes.
--- PAGE 2 ---

3. HR [ 15-20 candidates ]

This was a very chilled-out round. The interviewer asked me some standard HR questions:

1. Tell me about yourself

2. Tell me what you know about MSCI

3. What's your family background

4. Strengths and weaknesses

5. Hard work or Smart Work?

6. Why would you be a good candidate for MSCI

7. Where do you see yourself in 5 years?

8. Hobbies and interests

She then inquired if I had any questions for her, to which I asked a couple,

1. What do you look for in a candidate to be suitable for MSCI

2. How do you find MSCI workwise?

Lasted for about 30 minutes.
Selected a total of 8 Candidates

If you read this far (or skipped to the bottom), here are some tips that I followed (apart from the standard 'be
confident' and 'don't panic' stuff)

• Everytime I sat on the interview chair, the first thing on my mind was to follow the "SSS" strategy.

• SSS: Smile Slightly, Speak Slowly, Straight Back

• Treat the interviewer as your friend. Think as if this is a conversation and not an interview. You will

enjoy it and not stress unnecessarily.

• Make sure you know the name of the interviewer who took your interview. At times the next

interviewer asks ke pichla interview kisne liya and you not knowing it might create a bad impression.

• Show the interviewer that you are Smart & a Fast Learner.

• Fast Learner: For eg. If the job requires Python, you don't need to show that you know

python. You need to show that even when you don't know Python, learning it will be very
easy for you.

• Smart: For Eg. Even if you do not know a DSA question or a logical question, you are

thinking about it and giving it a shot. Nahi aaya toh thike but dimaag lagane ka try toh kar
rahe ho to get an answer.

• In the end if the interviewer asks if you have a question, it is much appreciated if you can take some

generalized topic from the interview itself and ask a question from it. That way it wont look scripted
and you would seem a curious person.

• The MCQs consisted of questions on:

• DSA (guess the output, trees, queue, stack - postfix/prefix etc)

• DBMS/SQL (identify incorrect query, common queries etc)

• OOPS (basic concepts)

• The Coding question was related to DFS.

• It was similar to the 'number of islands' question on leetcode with some minor modifications.

(Number of Islands - LeetCode)
49 students cleared the OA.
--- PAGE 2 ---

2. Technical Interview 1 [49 students appeared]

Started with the interviewer checking out my resume.
He then directly jumped me on my projects and asked me to explain one of them.
Pro Tip 1: Prepare beforehand about all your project's explanations. Have 3-4 points ready so that
you know what to speak when asked to explain your projects.
I explained my project, he cross questioned on why I used this particular tech stack.
Pro Tip 2: Don't just say the tech stack I used is better/faster blah blah. They want honest answers.
Tell them one advantage and tell them that you were more familiar with it than the other stack so you
used it. Generalize this approach of answering similar questions. HONESTY op.
He further asked me JavaScript & React.js questions, since I had a project made entirely with JavaScript and
one included React. I had used/heard some terms he asked me to explain, and some I had never heard of.
Pro Tip 3:
if(don't know the answer) ‹
while(heard of it but not able to recollect) {
cout < "Please give me a hint to recollect";
cout < "Nope, I haven't encountered this / heard of this";
He further asked me about my internship experiences. He took a bullet point "increased website loading
speed by xyz%", and asked me to explain how.
Pro Tip 4: 'Doing your resume' means preparing explanations for every single bullet point you have
written. No one is 100% honest about every single word on their resume. It is okay to lie a bit,
provided you have a backup ready. Prepare these beforehand so that you do not get trapped during
the interview, and LIMIT THE LIES.
He further asked me a DSA question. It was an even easier version of Valid Parentheses - LeetCode
I knew the question well, yet I asked him to verify my answer on some test cases.
Pro Tip 5: The first part of solving a question is to UNDERSTAND it. Take your time to understand
the question, take 1-2 sample test cases and verify the output with the interviewer, then proceed to
solve it.
I told him a brute-force approach. While dry-running, I told him the 'stack' approach, and explained to him
the reason why I am using a stack, and what I will do at every step. I took the given test case, and dry run the
approach to get the answer. I then modified the same test case to make him believe that this approach would
cover all possible cases. He was contended by my explanation and dry run, he didn't ask me to code.
The entire interview lasted for around 30 mins. 20 mins for the resume and 10 mins for the DSA question.
--- PAGE 3 ---
Technical Interview 2 [27 students appeared]
After waiting for almost 3 hours.. pheww.. I finally had my Tech Round 2. The interviewer (who was also
the VP of MSCI, which I didn't know then), took my resume and asked me to introduce myself.
Pro Tip 6: Prepare a sweet and short (40-50 sec) introduction. "What you say is important, but
"How" you say it will set the tone of the interview. Try to stand out while answering this.
He then took one of my projects and asked me to explain it. This was the same project I explained in Round

1. He asked very detailed questions such as how did I extract stuff from the database, where and how did I

store images etc. I was able to answer most of the questions, but got confused with one question. Took about
20 mins.
Pro Tip 7: Refer "Pro Tip 1'. Haa again.. I can not stress more on how important it is. If you are not
able to answer questions on your own project, that is a big red flag for the interviewer.
He then asked me a SQL question. "Suppose you have a table with millions or billions of rows, how would
you optimize searching for a particular entryằi
'. I didn't know the answer and I knew there must be a method
which I haven't studied. But unhe dikhana toh padega na ke you are capable of ideating and applying brains
to come up with a solution. I thought and tried it logically, and discussed it with him. He told me the solution
which is "Indexing". MSCI ne ye question last year bhi pucha tha jo meko ekdum se yaad ayaa.. Thanks to
the Interview Experience of my seniors (and TPO ofc). I cross-questioned to him, if this is similar to
hashmaps in C++ where you find by indexing in O(1). Vo kuch toh bole ispe and I definitely understood it
very clearly. Took about 5 mins.
Pro Tip 8: Ab pata nahi hai matlab ye nahi ke humehsa mana kardo. This question was logical, so try
to think about it first, and discuss it. Phir soch soch ke nahi aaya toh bolo IDK. You can also cross
question when he tells you the answer, but aisa lagna chahiye tumne dimaag lagaya isiliye you are
asking and not just for the sake.
He then gave me a DSA question. It was same as Linked List Cycle - LeetCode
I had solved this question kaafi pehele, but did not remember the optimal approach. Started with brute force
which I could think on the spot. (Traverse and change value to -1, if encountered -1 again then loop, or no
loop). I asked questions to him to clarify stuff, for eg. if I could modify the values of LinkedList etc. Then
meko slow-fast pointer wala approach strike hua while solving and discussing, which I told him and he was
happy with it and didn't ask me to code. Took about 10 mins.
Pro Tip 9: Ask questions to the interviewer when he gives you the problem. Take a test case and ask
ke ye sahi hai na, aise hi hoga na. Edge cases bhi puchlo. Let him think ke you are curious to solve it.
He then moved to the next DSA question. It was same as Remove Duplicates from Sorted Array - LeetCode
Sorted array sunte hi I thought of Binary Search. I took a test case and implemented it. He told me ke isse
kaise hoga try karke dekho, I tried so hard and got so far, but in the end BS se nahi hua. Wasted 10 mins on
it and then explained to him ke BS se kyu nahi hoga solve and it was silly 'sorted array' sunke hi BS use
kıya.
I asked for a hint, he told me swap karke try karo, I gave him a solution but he was quick to pick that it wont
work on another test case. Aur 10 mins gaye isme.
--- PAGE 4 ---
I feel he didn't explain the entire question properly. At this point he said that it is okay if you can throw the
duplicates at the end of the array.
I asked for another hint, he told me to use the 2 pointer approach, and then try to swap. I thought for a while,
then called him back and dry ran a test case. I connected it with the approach I was telling him earlier jisko
vo mana kiya tha. He understood what I was thinking, and finally I showed him the proper solution. This
took nearly 15 mins. The whole Q2 took nearly 30 mins.
Pro Tip 10: Ask for hints if needed. Converse with the interviewer. Vo bahot time se interview le raha
hoga toh usko bore mat hone do.
He asked me if I had questions, I asked him a question related to databases and how MSCI uses them.

4. HR Interview [15 students appeared]

Immediately after Tech Round 2, I was called for the HR round. The HR connected online over MS Teams.
He introduced himself (one of the lines included him saying that he is not a 'tech guy'). He then asked me
the "Tell me about yourself' question. He asked the following questions:
'Explain me about your project"
Since he was not a tech guy, I only explained the working of a project and did not go into technical details
since he prolly wouldnt understand that and I would bore him. That's exactly what he wanted to test.
"Has there been a situation where you were doing a project and you thought of giving up midway? What did
you do?"
I explained my IIT internship experience where something similar happened. In the end I didn't give up and
finished the project. That 'never give up' attitude was what he was expecting.
Explain a team project and how the team members contributed
I explained my semester mini project where I lead the team of 3. I told him that I understood the skills of
every person and then delegated work accordingly. I went way too honest with him while answering the
contributions wala part which I wont type since baaki 2 log bhi padh sakte hai ye.
"What did you do 2 years during the c*vid lockdown?"
I included everything from studying 12 hrs a day for JEE.. yes :), to learning new skills in free time after
JEE, to enjoying watching aviation videos, that being my interest. I showed him diversity, and didnt get
stuck on one thing.
"Do you have any questions for me?"
I asked about the work culture at MSCI. He was happy to answer that since he said that he had received a lot
of standard technical questions earlier despite him saying that he was not a tech guy. The interview ended up
with him asking me my preferred job location:)
Finally 8 students got the offer.
--- PAGE 5 ---

customSections.title: Advice & Tips for Juniors
customSections.content:
If you read this far (or skipped to the bottom), here are some tips that I followed (apart from the standard 'be
confident' and 'don't panic' stuff)

• Everytime I sat on the interview chair, the first thing on my mind was to follow the "SSS" strategy.

• SSS: Smile Slightly, Speak Slowly, Straight Back

• Treat the interviewer as your friend. Think as if this is a conversation and not an interview. You will

enjoy it and not stress unnecessarily.

• Make sure you know the name of the interviewer who took your interview. At times the next

interviewer asks ke pichla interview kisne liya and you not knowing it might create a bad impression.

• Show the interviewer that you are Smart & a Fast Learner.

• Fast Learner: For eg. If the job requires Python, you don't need to show that you know

python. You need to show that even when you don't know Python, learning it will be very
easy for you.

• Smart: For Eg. Even if you do not know a DSA question or a logical question, you are

thinking about it and giving it a shot. Nahi aaya toh thike but dimaag lagane ka try toh kar
rahe ho to get an answer.

• In the end if the interviewer asks if you have a question, it is much appreciated if you can take some

generalized topic from the interview itself and ask a question from it. That way it wont look scripted
and you would seem a curious person.

Round 0 - Coding round (70 mins)

12 MCQs, 4 based on Java (Code snippets were giver and we had to predict the output). 4 based on
DBMS. 4 on analytical. 1 coding question. Similar to https://leetcode.com/problems/number-of-
islands/ .

Round 1 - Technical Interview (1 hr)

The interviewer was friendly. Started with 'Introduce yourself'. Scanned my resume thoroughly.
Asked to explain about my projects in depth. How did you use 3rd party APIs. How did you implement
different libraries in ML(Since one of my projects was based on ML). Switching to OOPS, What are
interfaces, what is encapsulation.
Then she jumped on DBMS. Asked me to write a query that given an employee table, give the details
of the employee having the second highest salary. What is LEFT JOIN. Difference between UNION and
UNION ALL. Difference between DELETE and TRUNCATE. Which one allows you to retrieve the
deleted data. I was not comfortable with this question so I clearly told that I don't know the answer.
Then she asked me how will you send an output generated by a java program to MySQL database. I
was not sure about the answer but a rough guess(I specifically mentioned that I am giving a rough
guess). A DSA question was asked, Given a sorted array, give the first and last occurrence of a
number.
Any questions for the interviewer. With this the round got over.

Round 2 - Technical Interview (30 to 40 mins)

What programming language do you use. What is a linked list. Show me the internal implementation
of a linked list. The interviewer handed me his laptop and told me to code. Build the list, insert,
delete, lookup. I was stuck at a couple of places but the interviewer helped me out. Then a couple of
OOPS questions were asked. Method overloading vs overriding. Then a puzzle was asked. Don't
underestimate puzzles.

Round 3 - HR round

Pretty chill round. Questions like strengths and weaknesses. Family background. How were the
previous 2 interviews. Do you know about the company? Full form of company. Situational questions
like if one of the teammates does not perform well, what will u do? Be honest and confident.

Placement Process Timeline:
15th July, 2023 - Resume Screening (Online Uploading of Resume)
17th July, 2023 - PPT, followed by Screening Test
19th July, 2023 - Offline Technical (2) + HR(1) Interviews held in College
Screening Test Round (Online)
This round was divided in 4 categories:-

• 4 MCQs on CS Fundamentals + Basic DS - Consisted of qs related to Infix/ Postfix

Notation.

• 4 MCQs on SQL - Touch upon basics of DBMS and SQL (W3Schools would be enough).

• 4 MCQs on specific Java Related Qs.

• 1 Coding Qs - Modification of

(https://leetcode.com/problems/number-of-islands/description/) instead of 1's and 0's
there were 4 alphabets a,b,c,d.
Offline Technical Round 1(40 minutes)
The interview started off directly with the interviewer asking me questions regarding the projects
I had listed. He was keen on knowing more about the techstacks, database softwares and tools
involved in the making of the project.
Next he switched to asking me questions about SQL and databases. He asked me indexing in
general, non-clustering indexing (I wasn't sure of the ans, so I broke down the word into two
parts, explained them individually), sharding, normalization techniques (specifically 3NF),
rollback and commit, and the difference between Truncate and Delete. He specifically asked if
truncating means losing data from the database completely. So I confidently told him yes,
however truncating signifies that the data is still present in the logs and can be retrieved.
He asked me questions on OOPs concepts, Encapsulation and Abstraction, and asked me to give
an example (he specifically mentioned something apart from the Car eg)
Lastly he asked me for a DSA qs- given a range limit (3) and a String, I have to find if there are
any duplicates in any contiguous substring of specified range limit. I started off with a
Brute-force approach of TC O(N^2) and eventually led up to an implementation with Hashmap
in ON) time. He asked me for an estimate of how many barbers do you think might be across
--- PAGE 2 ---
Mumbai. So I broke down to think about the number of barbers in my area and scaling up, but
then also listed three factors that I felt the number of barbers depended upon and gave him a
rough estimate of 100-120 (he was expecting more).
I asked him questions about MSCI, about the work they listed on the ppt, and he gave me an
insight on the restrictions too that employees have while working on teams involving Indexing
specifically.
Offline Technical Round 2(25 minutes)
I had a more senior interviewer for this round and he asked me to tell about myself. I had a ML
project on Latent Dirichlet Algorithm, so he asked me to explain the complete working of it on
paper, which I managed to do by drawing out diagrams. I had a project on a Travel Itinerary API
specification, which he was interested to know the JSON format in which I returned my Itinerary
object and even the logic of day-wise allocation of the places. Overall, it was an in-depth logic
analysis of each project. He even asked me to actually write down the JSON return object format
and any data structures I used for the same. It ended with me asking him about MSCI being
classified as a product-based or service-based company and his team and its current areas of
working. He was generous to give a detailed insight for the same.
HR Round (20 minutes)
The interviewer made me feel really comfortable. She asked me about my previous interviews,
(try asking and remember your interviewer names, it shows you're socially active), my domains
of interest. What are my strengths and weaknesses (try to mention something you're actively
working on). Like for this question, I mentioned to her that it was hard initially in project teams
to find someone you can relate to because everyone approaches the project with a different level
of priority towards a project, but with active communication, I have been trying to bridge the gap
and finding midway to achieve progress in my contribution to the project. Next she asked me
where do I see myself 5 years down the line and am I a team member or solo player. Be vocal
about preferences, if given a choice, ranging from location to interested domain. Lastly she asked
me about my family and their current job profiles.
Tips for the interview:-

• Be vocal. If something goes wrong, just acknowledge it.

• Be transparent to a degree where you know that the transparency isn't backfiring you.

• Be confident in your approach to DSA and even HR rounds.

ALL THE BEST!
